question: For the ACTIVE networks that have an RBAC permission action of 'access_as_shared', group results by network status and whether the network is “High Subnet Count” (its subnet total is more than one standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) above the mean subnet count across all such ACTIVE shared networks) or “Normal Subnet Count” otherwise. evidence: "access_as_shared" permission is predicated by "networkrbacs.action = 'access_as_shared'"
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT n.id AS network_id, SUM(1) AS total_subnets FROM NETWORKS AS n JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS r ON n.id = r.object_id JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON r.object_id = s.network_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' AND r.action = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.id HAVING SUM(1) > ( SELECT AVG(subnet_cnt) + STDDEV(subnet_cnt) FROM ( SELECT n2.id AS network_id, SUM(1) AS subnet_cnt FROM NETWORKS AS n2 JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS r2 ON n2.id = r2.object_id JOIN SUBNETS AS s2 ON r2.object_id = s2.network_id WHERE n2.status = 'ACTIVE' AND r2.action = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n2.id ) AS per_network ) ), NetworkSubnetCategory AS ( SELECT n.status, CASE WHEN ic.network_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'High Subnet Count' ELSE 'Normal Subnet Count' END AS subnet_count_category, COUNT(DISTINCT n.id) AS total_networks FROM NETWORKS n JOIN NETWORKRBACS r ON n.id = r.object_id LEFT JOIN inner_cte ic ON n.id = ic.network_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' AND r.action = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.status, subnet_count_category ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(status) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE status END AS status, CASE WHEN GROUPING(subnet_count_category) = 1 AND GROUPING(status) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE subnet_count_category END AS subnet_count_category, SUM(total_networks) AS total_networks FROM NetworkSubnetCategory GROUP BY status, subnet_count_category WITH ROLLUP;

question: For each port status, report the status and the range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the number of port security bindings per port, considering only ports that have at least one port security binding and belong to tenant ID '17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7', and also include the overall average number of port security bindings per port across those same ports. SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( SELECT p.status, MAX(ps.binding_count) - MIN(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_range, VARIANCE(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_variance, STDDEV(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_stddev FROM ports AS p JOIN ( SELECT p2.id AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS binding_count FROM ports AS p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings AS b ON p2.id = b.port_id WHERE p2.tenant_id IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') GROUP BY p2.id ) AS ps ON p.id = ps.port_id GROUP BY p.status ORDER BY binding_count_range DESC ) SELECT inner_cte.status, inner_cte.binding_count_range, inner_cte.binding_count_variance, inner_cte.binding_count_stddev, avg_bindings.avg_binding_count FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(binding_count) AS avg_binding_count FROM ( SELECT p2.id AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS binding_count FROM ports AS p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings AS b ON p2.id = b.port_id WHERE p2.tenant_id IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') GROUP BY p2.id ) AS sub ) AS avg_bindings ON 1 = 1 ORDER BY inner_cte.binding_count_range DESC;

question: For each ACTIVE network that has an RBAC permission action of 'access_as_shared', return the network ID and its total number of subnets, along with the overall benchmark threshold (mean subnet count plus one standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) across all such networks) and a usage category of 'ABOVE_THRESHOLD' or 'NOT_ABOVE_THRESHOLD'. SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT n.id AS network_id, SUM(1) AS total_subnets FROM NETWORKS AS n JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS r ON n.id = r.object_id JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON r.object_id = s.network_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' AND r.action = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.id HAVING SUM(1) > ( SELECT AVG(subnet_cnt) + STDDEV(subnet_cnt) FROM ( SELECT n2.id AS network_id, SUM(1) AS subnet_cnt FROM NETWORKS AS n2 JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS r2 ON n2.id = r2.object_id JOIN SUBNETS AS s2 ON r2.object_id = s2.network_id WHERE n2.status = 'ACTIVE' AND r2.action = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n2.id ) AS per_network )), benchmark_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(subnet_cnt) + STDDEV(subnet_cnt) AS threshold FROM ( SELECT n2.id AS network_id, SUM(1) AS subnet_cnt FROM NETWORKS AS n2 JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS r2 ON n2.id = r2.object_id JOIN SUBNETS AS s2 ON r2.object_id = s2.network_id WHERE n2.status = 'ACTIVE' AND r2.action = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n2.id ) AS per_network ) SELECT i.network_id, i.total_subnets, b.threshold AS benchmark_threshold, CASE WHEN i.total_subnets > b.threshold THEN 'ABOVE_THRESHOLD' ELSE 'NOT_ABOVE_THRESHOLD' END AS subnet_usage_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN benchmark_cte b;

SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (SELECT lb.OPERATING_STATUS, SUM(s.BYTES_IN) AS total_bytes_in FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS s ON lb.ID = s.LOADBALANCER_ID WHERE lb.PROVISIONING_STATUS = 'ACTIVE' AND lb.VIP_SUBNET_ID IN ( SELECT subnets.id FROM subnets JOIN networks ON networks.id = subnets.network_id WHERE networks.id NOT IN ( SELECT networkrbacs.object_id FROM networkrbacs WHERE networkrbacs.action = 'access_as_shared' AND (networkrbacs.target_tenant = '*' OR networkrbacs.target_tenant = '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b') ) ) GROUP BY lb.OPERATING_STATUS HAVING SUM(s.BYTES_IN) > 1000000) SELECT lb.TENANT_ID, MAX(inner_cte.total_bytes_in) AS max_total_bytes_in_across_statuses FROM inner_cte JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb ON lb.OPERATING_STATUS = inner_cte.OPERATING_STATUS WHERE lb.PROVISIONING_STATUS = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY lb.TENANT_ID HAVING MAX(inner_cte.total_bytes_in) > 1000000;

question: For each IPv4 subnet whose subnet ID is in ('012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48'), show the subnet name, tenant ID, network ID, IP version, CIDR, gateway IP, DHCP enabled flag, the allocation pool’s first IP and last IP, and the maximum subnet standard attribute ID considering the current row and the next 2 rows when ordered by subnet ID. SQL: SELECT s.NAME, s.TENANT_ID, s.NETWORK_ID, s.IP_VERSION, s.CIDR, s.GATEWAY_IP, s.ENABLE_DHCP, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, MAX(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( ORDER BY s.ID ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS AS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 AND s.ID IN ('012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48');

question: For each port status and device owner, considering only ports whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports' and excluding shared networks (i.e., networks whose IDs appear in networkrbacs with action = 'access_as_shared' and target_tenant = '*' or '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b'), return the number of ports and the earliest (minimum) standard attribute updated timestamp. SQL: SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' AND p.NETWORK_ID NOT IN ( SELECT networkrbacs.object_id FROM networkrbacs WHERE networkrbacs.action = 'access_as_shared' AND (networkrbacs.target_tenant = '*' OR networkrbacs.target_tenant = '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b') ) GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER;

question: For each security group, return the security group ID and the total number of ports bound to it, considering only ports whose admin_state_up is 1, excluding ports on shared networks (i.e., networks.id NOT IN (SELECT networkrbacs.object_id FROM networkrbacs WHERE networkrbacs.action = 'access_as_shared' AND (networkrbacs.target_tenant = '*' OR networkrbacs.target_tenant = '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b'))), and only include security groups whose total bound-port count is more than one standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) above the mean bound-port count across all security groups. SQL: SELECT sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, SUM(CASE WHEN p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS total_ports_up FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID JOIN NETWORKS AS n ON p.NETWORK_ID = n.ID WHERE n.ID NOT IN ( SELECT networkrbacs.object_id FROM networkrbacs WHERE networkrbacs.action = 'access_as_shared' AND (networkrbacs.target_tenant = '*' OR networkrbacs.target_tenant = '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b') ) GROUP BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > ( SELECT AVG(port_cnt) + STDDEV(port_cnt) FROM ( SELECT sgpb2.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, SUM(CASE WHEN p2.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_cnt FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb2 JOIN PORTS AS p2 ON sgpb2.PORT_ID = p2.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb2 ON p2.ID = psb2.PORT_ID JOIN NETWORKS AS n2 ON p2.NETWORK_ID = n2.ID WHERE n2.ID NOT IN ( SELECT networkrbacs.object_id FROM networkrbacs WHERE networkrbacs.action = 'access_as_shared' AND (networkrbacs.target_tenant = '*' OR networkrbacs.target_tenant = '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b') ) GROUP BY sgpb2.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ) AS per_sg );

question: For each network status, show the status and compute the average, range (max minus min), and variance of the network MTU values for networks that have an RBAC rule with action = 'access_as_shared' and that are publicly shared (i.e., the RBAC target tenant is '*'). question: For each subnet (by subnet name), show the range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the number of IP allocation pools per subnet, considering only subnets that have at least one DNS nameserver entry and excluding shared networks (i.e., networks whose IDs appear in networkrbacs with action = 'access_as_shared' and target_tenant = '*' or '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b'). SQL: SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(pool_count) - MIN(pool_count) AS pool_count_range, VARIANCE(pool_count) AS pool_count_variance, STDDEV(pool_count) AS pool_count_stddev FROM subnets AS s JOIN dnsnameservers AS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id JOIN ( SELECT s2.id AS subnet_id, COUNT(*) AS pool_count FROM subnets AS s2 JOIN ipallocationpools AS p ON p.subnet_id = s2.id GROUP BY s2.id, p.id ) AS pool_stats ON pool_stats.subnet_id = s.id JOIN networks AS n ON n.id = s.network_id WHERE n.id NOT IN ( SELECT networkrbacs.object_id FROM networkrbacs WHERE networkrbacs.action = 'access_as_shared' AND (networkrbacs.target_tenant = '*' OR networkrbacs.target_tenant = '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b') ) GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY pool_count_range DESC;

question: For each network status, show the status and compute both the variance and the standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the security group binding order (PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED) across networks that have at least one security binding, excluding shared networks (i.e., networks whose IDs appear in NETWORKRBACS with action = 'access_as_shared' and target_tenant = '*' or '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b'). SQL: SELECT n.STATUS AS network_status, VARIANCE(nsb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED) AS port_security_enabled_variance, STDDEV(nsb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED) AS port_security_enabled_stddev FROM NETWORKS AS n JOIN NETWORKSECURITYBINDINGS AS nsb ON n.ID = nsb.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ID NOT IN ( SELECT networkrbacs.object_id FROM networkrbacs WHERE networkrbacs.action = 'access_as_shared' AND (networkrbacs.target_tenant = '*' OR networkrbacs.target_tenant = '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b') ) GROUP BY n.STATUS ORDER BY port_security_enabled_variance DESC;

question: For each network status, show the status and compute the average and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the network MTU values, considering only networks that have an associated security binding and an RBAC entry with action = 'access_as_shared', and excluding shared networks (i.e., exclude networks whose ID appears in networkrbacs with action = 'access_as_shared' and target_tenant = '*' or '9f13bf11e06e4d81b44c8c3e62d4362b'). evidence: Subnet ID "012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48" is predicated by "subnets.id IN ('012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48')" Subnet ID "0807c5b3-aa6c-4108-8884-7b4948a19178" is predicated by "subnets.id IN ('0807c5b3-aa6c-4108-8884-7b4948a19178')" Subnet ID "0814cd95-6c95-4669-8415-e555344bb15b" is predicated by "subnets.id IN ('0814cd95-6c95-4669-8415-e555344bb15b')" Subnet ID "16eaae8c-1920-4b8b-8765-f149dde8a1a6" is predicated by "subnets.id IN ('16eaae8c-1920-4b8b-8765-f149dde8a1a6')" Subnet ID "1e360a1e-339a-4dc7-a250-28c31fcd905a" is predicated by "subnets.id IN ('1e360a1e-339a-4dc7-a250-28c31fcd905a')" Subnet ID "2019039a-089f-408c-b080-201a0c5cbe6f" is predicated by "subnets.id IN ('2019039a-089f-408c-b080-201a0c5cbe6f')" Subnet ID "25a309b3-7334-44b7-99b5-85a874d28475" is predicated by "subnets.id IN ('25a309b3-7334-44b7-99b5-85a874d28475')" Subnet ID "25e390e6-3a89-42d7-a5e8-c4da22edc587" is predicated by "subnets.id IN ('25e390e6-3a89-42d7-a5e8-c4da22edc587')" Subnet ID "26a23140-1cb7-4ccd-b2d7-50611eb82663" is predicated by "subnets.id IN ('26a23140-1cb7-4ccd-b2d7-50611eb82663')" Subnet ID "2f08159a-e945-4ba2-a583-431d1f8078d9" is predicated by "subnets.id IN ('2f08159a-e945-4ba2-a583-431d1f8078d9')"
SQL: SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, s.tenant_id, s.network_id, s.ip_version, s.cidr, s.gateway_ip, d.address AS dns_address, d.ORDER AS dns_order, p.first_ip, p.last_ip, MAX(d.ORDER) OVER ( ORDER BY s.id, d.ORDER ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS max_dns_order_next_2 FROM subnets AS s JOIN dnsnameservers AS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id JOIN ipallocationpools AS p ON p.subnet_id = s.id WHERE s.enable_dhcp = 1 AND s.id IN ( '012993ae-5d73-4aad-834b-e87a31e99d48', '0807c5b3-aa6c-4108-8884-7b4948a19178', '0814cd95-6c95-4669-8415-e555344bb15b', '16eaae8c-1920-4b8b-8765-f149dde8a1a6', '1e360a1e-339a-4dc7-a250-28c31fcd905a', '2019039a-089f-408c-b080-201a0c5cbe6f', '25a309b3-7334-44b7-99b5-85a874d28475', '25e390e6-3a89-42d7-a5e8-c4da22edc587', '26a23140-1cb7-4ccd-b2d7-50611eb82663', '2f08159a-e945-4ba2-a583-431d1f8078d9' );

question: For each port host, show the host name and compute the range and variance of the ports’ standard attribute IDs, considering only ports that have an IP allocation and whose IP address is in ('10.150.64.113/8'). Do not return any rounded answers.
evidence: IP Address "10.150.64.113/8" is predicated by "ipallocations.ip_address IN ('10.150.64.113/8')"
SQL: SELECT b.HOST, MAX(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) - MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_range, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE ia.PORT_ID IS NOT NULL AND ia.IP_ADDRESS IN ('10.150.64.113/8') GROUP BY b.HOST ORDER BY standard_attr_id_range DESC;

question: How many ports are currently in DOWN status, belong to the network with ID '0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d', have at least one extra DHCP option configured with IP version 4, and are also bound to a QoS port policy? Do not return any rounded answers.
evidence: Network ID "0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d" is predicated by "ports.network_id IN ('0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d')"
SQL: SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_ipv4_dhcpopt_and_qos_policy FROM QOS_PORT_POLICY_BINDINGS qppb JOIN PORTS p ON qppb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN EXTRADHCPOPTS e ON p.ID = e.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND e.IP_VERSION = 4 AND p.NETWORK_ID IN ('0a1d0a27-cffa-4de3-92c5-9d3fd3f2e74d');

question: For ports whose status is DOWN and whose device ID is `da811c75-0f9b-462c-b020-8ea55f6ca7c7`, list each port ID and the dense rank of that port when ordering by its port-security setting (PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED), using a window frame that includes the current row and the 2 preceding rows. Do not return any rounded answers.
evidence: Device ID "da811c75-0f9b-462c-b020-8ea55f6ca7c7" is predicated by "ports.device_id IN ('da811c75-0f9b-462c-b020-8ea55f6ca7c7')"
SQL: SELECT p.id AS port_id, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY psb.port_security_enabled ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM ports AS p JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' AND p.device_id IN ('da811c75-0f9b-462c-b020-8ea55f6ca7c7');

question: For each security group, show the security group ID and the geometric mean of the standard attribute IDs of the ports bound to that security group, considering only ports whose standard attribute ID is greater than 0 and whose tenant ID is `17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7`. Do not return any rounded answers.
evidence: Tenant ID "17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7" is predicated by "ports.tenant_id IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7')"
SQL: SELECT s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, EXP(AVG(LN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID))) AS geometric_mean_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID > 0 AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') GROUP BY s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY geometric_mean_standard_attr_id DESC;

question: For each RBAC action (restricted to the **access_as_shared** permission), show the action name and compute the average, range (max minus min), and variance of the subnet IP version for subnets whose network is referenced by that RBAC entry. Do not return any rounded answers.
evidence: "access_as_shared" permission is predicated by "networkrbacs.action = 'access_as_shared'"
SQL: SELECT n.ACTION AS rbac_action, AVG(s.IP_VERSION) AS avg_ip_version, MAX(s.IP_VERSION) - MIN(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_range, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION IN (4, 6) AND n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_range DESC;

question: For each port that is administratively up, belongs to tenant ID `17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7`, and has at least one IP allocation, list the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, the number of IP allocations on that port, and the total number of distinct subnets those IP allocations belong to. Do not return any rounded answers.
evidence: Tenant ID "17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7" is predicated by "ports.tenant_id IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7')"
SQL: SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(ia.ip_address) AS ip_allocation_count, COUNT(DISTINCT ia.subnet_id) AS distinct_subnet_count FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND ia.ip_address IS NOT NULL AND p.tenant_id IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7') GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN and whose tenant ID is in ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7'), show the port ID, tenant ID, and MAC address, along with the running sum of the standard attribute IDs within each resource type group ordered by standard attribute ID. Do not return any rounded answers.
evidence: Tenant ID "17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7" is predicated by "ports.tenant_id IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7')"
SQL: SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER (PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND p.TENANT_ID IN ('17ea94ad74b64b9d92f4888336a598c7');

question: For the security group ID 0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c, list only the networks where more than 50% of the ports bound to that security group are in DOWN status, returning the network ID, total bound ports, total DOWN ports, and the DOWN-to-total ratio.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH Subq1 AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.STATUS AS port_status, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c' ), Subq2 AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY psb.port_security_enabled ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM ports AS p JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' ), PortNetwork AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID WHERE sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c' ) SELECT pn.network_id, COUNT(DISTINCT s1.port_id) AS total_ports_in_security_group, COUNT(DISTINCT s2.port_id) AS total_down_ports, ROUND( COUNT(DISTINCT s2.port_id) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT s1.port_id), 0), 2 ) AS down_port_ratio FROM PortNetwork pn LEFT JOIN Subq1 s1 ON s1.port_id = pn.port_id LEFT JOIN Subq2 s2 ON s2.port_id = pn.port_id GROUP BY pn.network_id ) SELECT network_id, total_ports_in_security_group, total_down_ports, down_port_ratio FROM inner_cte WHERE total_ports_in_security_group > 0 AND down_port_ratio > 0.50;

question: From the top 10 tenants (by number of qualifying subnets) where the qualifying subnets are IP version 4 and are on networks with an RBAC action of 'access_as_shared' (and whose subnet name/gateway IP group has a maximum IP version greater than 3), show each tenant’s ID, the total number of qualifying subnets, and whether they have any qualifying subnet whose maximum-IP-version-to-window-rank ratio (rounded to 2 decimals) is at least 2.00.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH SubnetWindowRanks AS ( SELECT s.NAME, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY sa.UPDATED_AT ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES AS sa ON sa.ID = s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ), SharedNetworkSubnetMaxIP AS ( SELECT s.name, MAX(s.ip_version) AS max_ip_version, s.gateway_ip FROM NETWORKRBACS n JOIN SUBNETS s ON n.object_id = s.network_id WHERE n.action = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY s.name, s.gateway_ip HAVING MAX(s.ip_version) > 3 ) SELECT swr.NAME AS subnet_name, swr.window_column, sns.gateway_ip, sns.max_ip_version, ROUND(sns.max_ip_version / NULLIF(swr.window_column, 0), 2) AS max_ip_version_per_window_rank FROM SubnetWindowRanks swr JOIN SharedNetworkSubnetMaxIP sns ON sns.name = swr.NAME ORDER BY max_ip_version_per_window_rank DESC ) SELECT s.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT s.id) AS total_qualifying_subnets, CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN inner_cte.max_ip_version_per_window_rank >= 2.00 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_ratio_at_least_2 FROM inner_cte JOIN subnets s ON s.name = inner_cte.subnet_name AND s.gateway_ip = inner_cte.gateway_ip GROUP BY s.tenant_id ORDER BY total_qualifying_subnets DESC LIMIT 10;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN, list the port ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and the row number ordered by IP address (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row), and also include the DOWN-status range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the number of port security bindings per port (considering only ports that have at least one port security binding), along with the total number of DOWN ports per tenant and the average number of DOWN ports across all tenants. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH DownPortsWithIPs AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), PortStatusSecurityBindingStats AS (SELECT p.status, MAX(ps.binding_count) - MIN(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_range, VARIANCE(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_variance, STDDEV(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_stddev FROM ports AS p JOIN ( SELECT p2.id AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS binding_count FROM ports AS p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings AS b ON p2.id = b.port_id GROUP BY p2.id ) AS ps ON p.id = ps.port_id GROUP BY p.status ORDER BY binding_count_range DESC) SELECT d.port_id, d.tenant_id, d.host, d.vif_type, d.ip_address, d.window_column, s.binding_count_range, s.binding_count_variance, s.binding_count_stddev FROM DownPortsWithIPs d JOIN PortStatusSecurityBindingStats s ON s.status = 'DOWN' ORDER BY d.ip_address), avg_down_ports AS ( SELECT AVG(down_port_count) AS avg_down_port_count FROM ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS down_port_count FROM ports WHERE status = 'DOWN' GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS sub ), tenant_down_counts AS ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS total_down_ports FROM ports WHERE status = 'DOWN' GROUP BY tenant_id ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.host, i.vif_type, i.ip_address, i.window_column, i.binding_count_range, i.binding_count_variance, i.binding_count_stddev, tdc.total_down_ports, adp.avg_down_port_count FROM inner_cte i JOIN tenant_down_counts tdc ON tdc.tenant_id = i.tenant_id JOIN avg_down_ports adp ON 1 = 1 ORDER BY i.ip_address;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN, list the port ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and the row number ordered by IP address (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row), along with the DOWN-status range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the number of port security bindings per port (considering only ports that have at least one port security binding). Additionally, only keep ports whose tenant has more DOWN ports than the average number of DOWN ports per tenant, and show each port’s total DOWN-port count for its tenant. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH DownPortsWithIPs AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), PortStatusSecurityBindingStats AS (SELECT p.status, MAX(ps.binding_count) - MIN(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_range, VARIANCE(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_variance, STDDEV(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_stddev FROM ports AS p JOIN ( SELECT p2.id AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS binding_count FROM ports AS p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings AS b ON p2.id = b.port_id GROUP BY p2.id ) AS ps ON p.id = ps.port_id GROUP BY p.status ORDER BY binding_count_range DESC) SELECT d.port_id, d.tenant_id, d.host, d.vif_type, d.ip_address, d.window_column, s.binding_count_range, s.binding_count_variance, s.binding_count_stddev FROM DownPortsWithIPs d JOIN PortStatusSecurityBindingStats s ON s.status = 'DOWN' ORDER BY d.ip_address), TenantDownPortCounts AS ( SELECT p.tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS down_port_count FROM ports p WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.tenant_id ), AvgDownPortsPerTenant AS ( SELECT AVG(down_port_count) AS avg_down_ports FROM TenantDownPortCounts ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.host, i.vif_type, i.ip_address, i.window_column, i.binding_count_range, i.binding_count_variance, i.binding_count_stddev, t.down_port_count FROM inner_cte i JOIN TenantDownPortCounts t ON t.tenant_id = i.tenant_id WHERE t.down_port_count > (SELECT avg_down_ports FROM AvgDownPortsPerTenant) ORDER BY i.ip_address;

question: For ports that are DOWN and are also bound to the security group ID 0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c, show the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, port status, and allocated IP address, along with (1) the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within each security group (ordered by standard attribute ID) and (2) the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within each network (ordered by standard attribute ID). Additionally, for each tenant appearing in these results, include the total number of ports they own and the average number of ports across all tenants. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH Subq1 AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), Subq2 AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.STATUS AS port_status, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c' ) SELECT s1.port_id, s1.tenant_id, s1.mac_address, s2.port_status, s2.ip_address, s1.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_security_group, s2.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_network FROM Subq1 s1 JOIN Subq2 s2 ON s1.port_id = s2.port_id ORDER BY s1.port_id) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.port_status, i.ip_address, i.running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_security_group, i.running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_network, COUNT(p_all.id) AS total_ports_for_tenant, avg_ports.avg_port_count AS avg_ports_across_all_tenants FROM inner_cte i JOIN ports p_all ON p_all.tenant_id = i.tenant_id JOIN (SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_port_count FROM (SELECT COUNT(id) AS port_count FROM ports GROUP BY tenant_id) AS sub) AS avg_ports GROUP BY i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.port_status, i.ip_address, i.running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_security_group, i.running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_network, avg_ports.avg_port_count ORDER BY i.port_id;

question: Among the networks returned by the top-3 shared-subnet analysis (RBAC action = 'access_as_shared') that are also ACTIVE and have an ACTIVE total subnet count more than one standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) above the mean across all ACTIVE networks, show each network’s ID, the shared subnet count, the ACTIVE total subnet count, the ACTIVE-to-shared subnet ratio (rounded to 2 decimals), and whether the network’s tenant has any other ACTIVE networks besides this one.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH ActiveHighSubnetNetworks AS ( SELECT n.id AS network_id, SUM(1) AS total_subnets FROM NETWORKS AS n JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS r ON n.id = r.object_id JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON r.object_id = s.network_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY n.id HAVING SUM(1) > ( SELECT AVG(subnet_cnt) + STDDEV(subnet_cnt) FROM ( SELECT n2.id AS network_id, SUM(1) AS subnet_cnt FROM NETWORKS AS n2 JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS r2 ON n2.id = r2.object_id JOIN SUBNETS AS s2 ON r2.object_id = s2.network_id WHERE n2.status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY n2.id ) AS per_network ) ), TopSharedNetworks AS ( SELECT n.OBJECT_ID AS network_id, COUNT(*) AS subnet_count FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.OBJECT_ID ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 3 ) SELECT tsn.network_id, tsn.subnet_count AS shared_subnet_count, ahsn.total_subnets AS active_total_subnets, ROUND(ahsn.total_subnets / NULLIF(tsn.subnet_count, 0), 2) AS Active_to_Shared_Subnet_Ratio FROM TopSharedNetworks tsn JOIN ActiveHighSubnetNetworks ahsn ON ahsn.network_id = tsn.network_id ORDER BY Active_to_Shared_Subnet_Ratio DESC ) SELECT i.network_id, i.shared_subnet_count, i.active_total_subnets, i.Active_to_Shared_Subnet_Ratio, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT n_other.id) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS tenant_has_other_active_networks FROM inner_cte i JOIN NETWORKS n_self ON n_self.id = i.network_id LEFT JOIN NETWORKS n_other ON n_other.tenant_id = n_self.tenant_id AND n_other.status = 'ACTIVE' AND n_other.id <> n_self.id GROUP BY i.network_id, i.shared_subnet_count, i.active_total_subnets, i.Active_to_Shared_Subnet_Ratio ORDER BY i.Active_to_Shared_Subnet_Ratio DESC, i.active_total_subnets DESC;

question: For each IPv4 subnet that has a positive average DNS nameserver order, show the subnet name, tenant ID, network ID, IP version, CIDR, gateway IP, DHCP enabled flag, allocation pool first and last IP, the maximum subnet standard attribute ID over the current row and next 2 rows (ordered by subnet ID), the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of DNS nameserver order values for that subnet, and keep only those subnets whose coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) is greater than the average coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) across all such IPv4 subnets; order the results by the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) descending. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH SubnetPoolWindowStats AS ( SELECT s.NAME, s.TENANT_ID, s.NETWORK_ID, s.IP_VERSION, s.CIDR, s.GATEWAY_IP, s.ENABLE_DHCP, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, MAX(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( ORDER BY s.ID ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS AS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ), SubnetDnsOrderVariation AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, STDDEV(d.ORDER) / NULLIF(AVG(d.ORDER), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM subnets AS s JOIN dnsnameservers AS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id JOIN ipallocationpools AS p ON p.subnet_id = s.id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name HAVING AVG(d.ORDER) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ) SELECT spws.NAME AS subnet_name, spws.TENANT_ID, spws.NETWORK_ID, spws.IP_VERSION, spws.CIDR, spws.GATEWAY_IP, spws.ENABLE_DHCP, spws.FIRST_IP, spws.LAST_IP, spws.max_standard_attr_id_next2, sdov.coefficient_of_variation FROM SubnetPoolWindowStats spws JOIN SubnetDnsOrderVariation sdov ON spws.NAME = sdov.subnet_name ORDER BY sdov.coefficient_of_variation DESC) SELECT i.subnet_name, i.tenant_id, i.network_id, i.ip_version, i.cidr, i.gateway_ip, i.enable_dhcp, i.first_ip, i.last_ip, i.max_standard_attr_id_next2, i.coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte i WHERE i.coefficient_of_variation > (SELECT AVG(i2.coefficient_of_variation) FROM inner_cte i2) ORDER BY i.coefficient_of_variation DESC;

question: For IPv4 subnets that have more than 5 DNS nameserver entries, list each subnet name along with the range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the DNS nameserver order values configured for that subnet, and also include how far that subnet’s order range deviates from the average order range across all IPv4 subnets. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH SubnetOrderRangeVariance AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(d.ORDER) - MIN(d.ORDER) AS order_range, VARIANCE(d.ORDER) AS order_variance FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.id = d.subnet_id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY order_range DESC ), SubnetOrderStddevOver5 AS ( SELECT s.name, STDDEV(d.ORDER) AS order_stddev FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.id = d.subnet_id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name HAVING COUNT(*) > 5 ORDER BY order_stddev DESC ) SELECT sorv.subnet_name, sorv.order_range, sorv.order_variance, sos.order_stddev FROM SubnetOrderRangeVariance sorv JOIN SubnetOrderStddevOver5 sos ON sorv.subnet_name = sos.name), AverageOrderRange AS ( SELECT AVG(order_range) AS avg_order_range FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.subnet_name, i.order_range, i.order_variance, i.order_stddev, (i.order_range - aor.avg_order_range) AS deviation_from_avg_order_range FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN AverageOrderRange aor;

question: For the top 10 tenants with the most DOWN ports (considering only DOWN ports that have an IP allocation and at least one port security binding), show each tenant’s ID, total number of such DOWN ports, whether they have any floating IPs allocated to those ports, and also include the DOWN-status range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the number of port security bindings per port. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH DownPortsWithIPs AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), PortStatusSecurityBindingStats AS (SELECT p.status, MAX(ps.binding_count) - MIN(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_range, VARIANCE(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_variance, STDDEV(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_stddev FROM ports AS p JOIN ( SELECT p2.id AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS binding_count FROM ports AS p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings AS b ON p2.id = b.port_id GROUP BY p2.id ) AS ps ON p.id = ps.port_id GROUP BY p.status ORDER BY binding_count_range DESC) SELECT d.port_id, d.tenant_id, d.host, d.vif_type, d.ip_address, d.window_column, s.binding_count_range, s.binding_count_variance, s.binding_count_stddev FROM DownPortsWithIPs d JOIN PortStatusSecurityBindingStats s ON s.status = 'DOWN' ORDER BY d.ip_address) SELECT i.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT i.port_id) AS total_down_ports_with_ip_and_psb, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT f.id) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_floating_ips, MAX(i.binding_count_range) AS down_binding_count_range, MAX(i.binding_count_variance) AS down_binding_count_variance, MAX(i.binding_count_stddev) AS down_binding_count_stddev FROM inner_cte i JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = i.port_id LEFT JOIN floatingips f ON f.fixed_port_id = i.port_id GROUP BY i.tenant_id ORDER BY total_down_ports_with_ip_and_psb DESC LIMIT 10;

question: For ports whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports' and that are in status 'DOWN' with an IP allocation, list each port status, device owner, and binding host along with (a) the total number of ports and the earliest standard-attribute updated timestamp for that same status/owner group, and (b) the variance of STANDARD_ATTR_ID for that host. Do not repeat the port status if it is the same as the previous row, and include a subtotal row per port status. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH PortStatusOwnerStats AS (SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER), HostStandardAttrVariance AS (SELECT b.HOST, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND ia.PORT_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY b.HOST ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC), DownPortsWithIPAndPortsResourceType AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, b.HOST FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' AND p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND ia.PORT_ID IS NOT NULL ) SELECT d.port_status, d.device_owner, psos.port_count, psos.earliest_standard_attr_update, d.host, hsav.standard_attr_id_variance FROM DownPortsWithIPAndPortsResourceType d JOIN PortStatusOwnerStats psos ON psos.port_status = d.port_status AND psos.device_owner = d.device_owner JOIN HostStandardAttrVariance hsav ON hsav.HOST = d.host ORDER BY d.port_status, d.device_owner, hsav.standard_attr_id_variance DESC, d.host) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(port_status) OVER (ORDER BY port_status_sort, port_status, device_owner, standard_attr_id_variance DESC, host) = port_status THEN NULL ELSE port_status END AS port_status, device_owner, total_ports, earliest_standard_attr_update, host, standard_attr_id_variance FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.port_status) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE i.port_status END AS port_status_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.port_status) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE i.port_status END AS port_status, i.device_owner AS device_owner, COUNT(*) AS total_ports, MIN(i.earliest_standard_attr_update) AS earliest_standard_attr_update, i.host AS host, i.standard_attr_id_variance AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM inner_cte i GROUP BY i.port_status, i.device_owner, i.host, i.standard_attr_id_variance WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY port_status_sort, port_status, device_owner, standard_attr_id_variance DESC, host;

question: For each tenant, report the number of ports that are both DOWN (using a running sum of STANDARD_ATTR_ID within each security group) and administratively up (including port security binding counts and total enabled port security), show the average of this count across all tenants as a benchmark, and categorize each tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% above average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% below average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH down_ports_window AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), admin_up_ports_security AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ) SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_admin_up_security_count FROM down_ports_window dpw JOIN admin_up_ports_security aups ON dpw.port_id = aups.port_id AND dpw.tenant_id = aups.tenant_id AND dpw.mac_address = aups.mac_address), TenantDownAdminUpCounts AS ( SELECT p.tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS total_matching_ports FROM ports p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON psb.port_id = p.id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' AND p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.tenant_id ), AverageTenantCount AS ( SELECT AVG(total_matching_ports) AS avg_matching_ports FROM TenantDownAdminUpCounts ) SELECT t.tenant_id, t.total_matching_ports, a.avg_matching_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN t.total_matching_ports > a.avg_matching_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN t.total_matching_ports < a.avg_matching_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category, inner_cte.down_ports_with_admin_up_security_count AS overall_matching_ports_count FROM TenantDownAdminUpCounts t CROSS JOIN AverageTenantCount a CROSS JOIN inner_cte;

question: For each port status and device owner (considering only ports whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports'), show the total number of ports and the earliest standard-attribute updated timestamp, along with the number of administratively-up ports and the total count of port-security bindings and enabled port-security occurrences across those admin-up ports; then return only those (status, owner) groups whose total port count is greater than the average port count across all such (status, owner) groups. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH subq1 AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), subq2 AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ), subq2_rollup AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT s2.port_id) AS admin_up_port_count, SUM(s2.binding_count) AS total_binding_count, SUM(s2.port_security_enabled_total) AS total_port_security_enabled FROM subq2 s2 JOIN PORTS p ON p.ID = s2.port_id JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ) SELECT s1.port_status, s1.device_owner, s1.port_count, s1.earliest_standard_attr_update, COALESCE(r.admin_up_port_count, 0) AS admin_up_port_count, COALESCE(r.total_binding_count, 0) AS total_binding_count, COALESCE(r.total_port_security_enabled, 0) AS total_port_security_enabled FROM subq1 s1 LEFT JOIN subq2_rollup r ON r.port_status = s1.port_status AND r.device_owner = s1.device_owner ORDER BY s1.port_count DESC ) SELECT inner_cte.port_status, inner_cte.device_owner, inner_cte.port_count, inner_cte.earliest_standard_attr_update, inner_cte.admin_up_port_count, inner_cte.total_binding_count, inner_cte.total_port_security_enabled FROM inner_cte WHERE inner_cte.port_count > (SELECT AVG(port_count) FROM inner_cte) ORDER BY inner_cte.port_count DESC;

question: For each VIF type among ports that are DOWN, list the VIF type, total number of distinct DOWN ports, the average of the MAC-address-based admin_state_up window metric, the maximum IP-address-based row-number window value, and the number of distinct tenants, but only return VIF types whose total number of distinct DOWN ports is greater than the average total number of distinct DOWN ports across all VIF types (computed from the same DOWN-port MAC/IP joined results). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH PortDownMacWindow AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ), PortDownIpRowNumber AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT p2.vif_type, COUNT(DISTINCT p2.port_id) AS Total_Down_Ports, AVG(p1.window_column) AS Avg_AdminStateUp_Window_Across_Ports, MAX(p2.window_column) AS Max_Ip_RowNumber_Window, COUNT(DISTINCT p2.tenant_id) AS Distinct_Tenants FROM PortDownIpRowNumber p2 JOIN PortDownMacWindow p1 ON p1.HOST = p2.host AND p1.VIF_TYPE = p2.vif_type GROUP BY p2.vif_type ORDER BY Total_Down_Ports DESC) SELECT vif_type, Total_Down_Ports, Avg_AdminStateUp_Window_Across_Ports, Max_Ip_RowNumber_Window, Distinct_Tenants FROM inner_cte WHERE Total_Down_Ports > (SELECT AVG(Total_Down_Ports) FROM inner_cte) ORDER BY Total_Down_Ports DESC;

question: For DOWN ports, list the tenant ID, the tenant’s total number of DOWN ports and average admin_state_up (rounded), along with each port’s security group ID and rank within that security group (by port ID), plus the port name, MAC address, admin_state_up flag, binding host, VIF type, the 2-preceding-to-2-following VIF-type window average of admin_state_up (ordered by MAC address), and the normalized ratio of that window average to the tenant’s average admin_state_up for DOWN ports; additionally, for each tenant include the tenant’s total number of ports (all statuses) and the average port count across all tenants.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH PortBindingsWindow AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ), SecurityGroupPortRank AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' ), TenantDownPortSummary AS ( SELECT p.tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS down_port_count, AVG(p.admin_state_up) AS avg_admin_state_up_down FROM PORTS p WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.tenant_id ) SELECT sgpr.tenant_id, tds.down_port_count, ROUND(tds.avg_admin_state_up_down, 2) AS avg_admin_state_up_down, sgpr.security_group_id, sgpr.port_id, pbw.NAME AS port_name, sgpr.mac_address, pbw.ADMIN_STATE_UP, pbw.HOST AS binding_host, pbw.VIF_TYPE, pbw.window_column AS avg_admin_state_up_viftype_mac_window, sgpr.window_column AS port_rank_within_security_group, ROUND( pbw.window_column / NULLIF(tds.avg_admin_state_up_down, 0), 2 ) AS normalized_viftype_window_vs_tenant_avg FROM SecurityGroupPortRank sgpr JOIN PortBindingsWindow pbw ON pbw.MAC_ADDRESS = sgpr.mac_address JOIN TenantDownPortSummary tds ON tds.tenant_id = sgpr.tenant_id ORDER BY normalized_viftype_window_vs_tenant_avg DESC, sgpr.security_group_id, sgpr.port_id) SELECT inner_cte.*, tp.total_ports_all_statuses, ap.avg_port_count_across_tenants FROM inner_cte JOIN (SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(id) AS total_ports_all_statuses FROM PORTS GROUP BY tenant_id) AS tp ON tp.tenant_id = inner_cte.tenant_id JOIN (SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_port_count_across_tenants FROM (SELECT COUNT(id) AS port_count FROM PORTS GROUP BY tenant_id) AS sub) AS ap ON 1 = 1 ORDER BY inner_cte.normalized_viftype_window_vs_tenant_avg DESC, inner_cte.security_group_id, inner_cte.port_id;

question: For each load balancer operating status that (1) has more than 1 load balancer associated with the “haproxy” provider and (2) has over 1,000,000 total incoming bytes among load balancers in ACTIVE provisioning status, return the operating status, the total number of haproxy-associated load balancers, the total incoming bytes, and the percentage of incoming bytes contributed by ACTIVE haproxy-associated load balancers (ACTIVE haproxy bytes_in divided by total ACTIVE bytes_in for that operating status). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH HapLoadBalancersByOpStatus AS ( SELECT lb.OPERATING_STATUS, COUNT(*) AS total_loadbalancers FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE pra.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy' GROUP BY lb.OPERATING_STATUS HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ), ActiveBytesInByOpStatus AS ( SELECT lb.OPERATING_STATUS, SUM(s.BYTES_IN) AS total_bytes_in FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS s ON lb.ID = s.LOADBALANCER_ID WHERE lb.PROVISIONING_STATUS = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY lb.OPERATING_STATUS HAVING SUM(s.BYTES_IN) > 1000000 ) SELECT h.OPERATING_STATUS, h.total_loadbalancers, a.total_bytes_in FROM HapLoadBalancersByOpStatus h JOIN ActiveBytesInByOpStatus a ON h.OPERATING_STATUS = a.OPERATING_STATUS ), ActiveHaproxyBytesByOpStatus AS ( SELECT lb.OPERATING_STATUS, SUM(s.BYTES_IN) AS haproxy_active_bytes_in FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS lb JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS s ON lb.ID = s.LOADBALANCER_ID WHERE pra.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy' AND lb.PROVISIONING_STATUS = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY lb.OPERATING_STATUS ) SELECT i.OPERATING_STATUS, i.total_loadbalancers, i.total_bytes_in, ah.haproxy_active_bytes_in, (ah.haproxy_active_bytes_in * 1.0 / NULLIF(i.total_bytes_in, 0)) AS haproxy_active_bytes_in_pct FROM inner_cte i JOIN ActiveHaproxyBytesByOpStatus ah ON i.OPERATING_STATUS = ah.OPERATING_STATUS;

question: For each ACTIVE network (including its ID, name, tenant ID, admin_state_up flag, MTU, standard-attribute updated_at timestamp, and a row number per tenant ordered by network name), find the maximum number of distinct administratively-up ports (on that same network and tenant) that share the same VIF type, considering only ports that have a port-security binding. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH AdminUpPorts AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, b.VNIC_TYPE, p.TENANT_ID, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 ), ActiveNetworks AS ( SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' ) SELECT an.network_id, an.network_name, an.tenant_id, an.admin_state_up, an.mtu, an.standard_attr_updated_at, an.window_column AS network_row_number_within_tenant, ap.PORT_ID, ap.HOST, ap.VIF_TYPE, ap.VNIC_TYPE, ap.MAC_ADDRESS, ap.STATUS AS port_status, ap.DEVICE_OWNER, ap.window_column AS avg_standard_attr_id_window_2_preceding_2_following FROM ActiveNetworks an JOIN AdminUpPorts ap ON ap.NETWORK_ID = an.network_id AND ap.TENANT_ID = an.tenant_id ) , VifTypePortCounts AS ( SELECT network_id, tenant_id, VIF_TYPE, COUNT(DISTINCT PORT_ID) AS admin_up_ports_in_vif_type FROM inner_cte GROUP BY network_id, tenant_id, VIF_TYPE ) SELECT network_id, tenant_id, MAX(admin_up_ports_in_vif_type) AS max_admin_up_ports_sharing_same_vif_type FROM VifTypePortCounts GROUP BY network_id, tenant_id;

question: Using the per-network-status security/port statistics query as a base, also break results out by whether the network is “External” (has a row in EXTERNALNETWORKS) or “Internal” (otherwise). For each (network status, external status) combination, return the variance and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED across networks with at least one security binding, the total number of ports (restricted to STANDARDATTRIBUTES where RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports'), and include subtotals per network status plus a grand total. Keep the device-owner port counts and earliest standard-attribute UPDATED_AT (for the matching port status) in the output as well. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH NetworkSecurityStats AS ( SELECT n.STATUS AS network_status, VARIANCE(nsb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED) AS port_security_enabled_variance, STDDEV(nsb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED) AS port_security_enabled_stddev FROM NETWORKS AS n JOIN NETWORKSECURITYBINDINGS AS nsb ON n.ID = nsb.NETWORK_ID GROUP BY n.STATUS ORDER BY port_security_enabled_variance DESC ), PortOwnerStats AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), NetworkPortCountsByStatus AS ( SELECT n.STATUS AS network_status, COUNT(p.ID) AS total_ports_in_status FROM NETWORKS n JOIN PORTS p ON p.NETWORK_ID = n.ID JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY n.STATUS ) SELECT nss.network_status, nss.port_security_enabled_variance, nss.port_security_enabled_stddev, npc.total_ports_in_status, pos.port_status, pos.device_owner, pos.port_count, pos.earliest_standard_attr_update FROM NetworkSecurityStats nss JOIN NetworkPortCountsByStatus npc ON nss.network_status = npc.network_status JOIN PortOwnerStats pos ON pos.port_status = nss.network_status ORDER BY npc.total_ports_in_status DESC, nss.port_security_enabled_variance DESC, pos.port_count DESC) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.network_status) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE i.network_status END AS network_status, CASE WHEN GROUPING(external_status) = 1 AND GROUPING(i.network_status) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' WHEN GROUPING(external_status) = 1 AND GROUPING(i.network_status) = 1 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE external_status END AS external_status, SUM(i.port_security_enabled_variance) AS sum_port_security_enabled_variance, SUM(i.port_security_enabled_stddev) AS sum_port_security_enabled_stddev, SUM(i.total_ports_in_status) AS sum_total_ports_in_status, i.port_status, i.device_owner, SUM(i.port_count) AS port_count, MIN(i.earliest_standard_attr_update) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM ( SELECT inner_cte.*, CASE WHEN en.network_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'External' ELSE 'Internal' END AS external_status FROM inner_cte JOIN NETWORKS n ON n.STATUS = inner_cte.network_status LEFT JOIN EXTERNALNETWORKS en ON en.NETWORK_ID = n.ID ) i GROUP BY i.network_status, external_status, i.port_status, i.device_owner WITH ROLLUP;

question: For the networks returned by the “top 3 shared networks that are ACTIVE and have an ACTIVE subnet count more than one standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) above the mean” logic, list each network’s ID and name, the shared subnet count, the ACTIVE total subnet count, the ratio of ACTIVE total subnets to shared subnet count (rounded to 2 decimals), and the percentage of that network’s subnets that have DHCP enabled (rounded to 2 decimals).
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH ActiveHighSubnetNetworks AS ( SELECT n.id AS network_id, SUM(1) AS total_subnets FROM NETWORKS AS n JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS r ON n.id = r.object_id JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON r.object_id = s.network_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY n.id HAVING SUM(1) > ( SELECT AVG(subnet_cnt) + STDDEV(subnet_cnt) FROM ( SELECT n2.id AS network_id, SUM(1) AS subnet_cnt FROM NETWORKS AS n2 JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS r2 ON n2.id = r2.object_id JOIN SUBNETS AS s2 ON r2.object_id = s2.network_id WHERE n2.status = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY n2.id ) AS per_network ) ), TopSharedNetworks AS ( SELECT n.OBJECT_ID AS network_id, COUNT(*) AS subnet_count FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.OBJECT_ID ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 3 ) SELECT tsn.network_id, tsn.subnet_count AS shared_subnet_count, ahsn.total_subnets AS active_total_subnets, ROUND(ahsn.total_subnets / NULLIF(tsn.subnet_count, 0), 2) AS Active_to_Shared_Subnet_Ratio FROM TopSharedNetworks tsn JOIN ActiveHighSubnetNetworks ahsn ON ahsn.network_id = tsn.network_id ORDER BY Active_to_Shared_Subnet_Ratio DESC) SELECT i.network_id, n.name AS network_name, i.shared_subnet_count, i.active_total_subnets, i.Active_to_Shared_Subnet_Ratio, ROUND( 100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN s.enable_dhcp = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(s.id), 0), 2 ) AS pct_subnets_with_dhcp_enabled FROM inner_cte i JOIN networks n ON n.id = i.network_id JOIN subnets s ON s.network_id = i.network_id GROUP BY i.network_id, n.name, i.shared_subnet_count, i.active_total_subnets, i.Active_to_Shared_Subnet_Ratio ORDER BY pct_subnets_with_dhcp_enabled DESC, i.Active_to_Shared_Subnet_Ratio DESC;

question: Among the top 10 tenants with the most DOWN ports, show each tenant’s ID, total DOWN-port count, and whether they have any ports bound with VIF type 'ovs'. For each tenant, also include the tenant’s average admin_state_up for DOWN ports (rounded) and the maximum normalized VIF-type window average vs. the tenant average (computed from the DOWN-port details).
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH PortBindingsWindow AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ), SecurityGroupPortRank AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' ), TenantDownPortSummary AS ( SELECT p.tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS down_port_count, AVG(p.admin_state_up) AS avg_admin_state_up_down FROM PORTS p WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.tenant_id ) SELECT sgpr.tenant_id, tds.down_port_count, ROUND(tds.avg_admin_state_up_down, 2) AS avg_admin_state_up_down, sgpr.security_group_id, sgpr.port_id, pbw.NAME AS port_name, sgpr.mac_address, pbw.ADMIN_STATE_UP, pbw.HOST AS binding_host, pbw.VIF_TYPE, pbw.window_column AS avg_admin_state_up_viftype_mac_window, sgpr.window_column AS port_rank_within_security_group, ROUND( pbw.window_column / NULLIF(tds.avg_admin_state_up_down, 0), 2 ) AS normalized_viftype_window_vs_tenant_avg FROM SecurityGroupPortRank sgpr JOIN PortBindingsWindow pbw ON pbw.MAC_ADDRESS = sgpr.mac_address JOIN TenantDownPortSummary tds ON tds.tenant_id = sgpr.tenant_id ORDER BY normalized_viftype_window_vs_tenant_avg DESC, sgpr.security_group_id, sgpr.port_id) SELECT i.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT i.port_id) AS total_down_ports, ROUND(AVG(i.avg_admin_state_up_down), 2) AS avg_admin_state_up_down, CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN i.vif_type = 'ovs' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_ovs_vif_type, MAX(i.normalized_viftype_window_vs_tenant_avg) AS max_normalized_viftype_window_vs_tenant_avg FROM inner_cte i GROUP BY i.tenant_id ORDER BY total_down_ports DESC LIMIT 10;

question: For IPv4 subnets that belong to networks with an RBAC action of 'access_as_shared', list the subnet name, CIDR, RBAC target tenant, the running sum of subnet standard attribute IDs within each IP version group ordered by standard attribute ID, and the dense rank of the subnet’s standard attribute ID ordered by the standard attribute updated-at timestamp (using the current row and 2 preceding rows). Do not repeat the subnet name if it is the same as the previous row. Also include a subtotal row per RBAC target tenant showing the count of distinct subnets. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH SharedRbacSubnets AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, n.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant, SUM(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY s.IP_VERSION ORDER BY s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' ), IPv4SubnetDenseRanks AS ( SELECT s.NAME, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY sa.UPDATED_AT ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES AS sa ON sa.ID = s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ) SELECT srs.subnet_name, srs.subnet_cidr, srs.rbac_target_tenant, srs.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_ip_version, idr.window_column AS dense_rank_by_standardattribute_updated_at_for_ipv4 FROM SharedRbacSubnets AS srs JOIN IPv4SubnetDenseRanks AS idr ON idr.NAME = srs.subnet_name) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(subnet_name) OVER (ORDER BY rbac_target_tenant_sort, subnet_name_sort, subnet_name) = subnet_name THEN NULL ELSE subnet_name END AS subnet_name, subnet_cidr, rbac_target_tenant, running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_ip_version, dense_rank_by_standardattribute_updated_at_for_ipv4, distinct_subnets_in_target_tenant FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.rbac_target_tenant) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE i.rbac_target_tenant END AS rbac_target_tenant_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.subnet_name) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE i.subnet_name END AS subnet_name_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.rbac_target_tenant) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE i.rbac_target_tenant END AS rbac_target_tenant, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.subnet_name) = 1 THEN NULL ELSE i.subnet_name END AS subnet_name, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.subnet_name) = 1 THEN NULL ELSE i.subnet_cidr END AS subnet_cidr, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.subnet_name) = 1 THEN NULL ELSE i.running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_ip_version END AS running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_ip_version, CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.subnet_name) = 1 THEN NULL ELSE i.dense_rank_by_standardattribute_updated_at_for_ipv4 END AS dense_rank_by_standardattribute_updated_at_for_ipv4, COUNT(DISTINCT i.subnet_name) AS distinct_subnets_in_target_tenant FROM inner_cte AS i GROUP BY i.rbac_target_tenant, i.subnet_name, i.subnet_cidr, i.running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_ip_version, i.dense_rank_by_standardattribute_updated_at_for_ipv4 WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY rbac_target_tenant_sort, subnet_name_sort, subnet_name;

question: For each tenant that has at least one port which is admin_state_up = 1, bound to at least one security group, and has status DOWN, list the tenant ID, the number of such qualifying ports they have, and the average number of such qualifying ports across all tenants. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH SecurityGroupBoundPorts AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name), DownPortBindings AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT sgp.tenant_id, sgp.port_id, sgp.port_name, sgp.security_group_binding_count, sgp.dns_record_count, dpb.host, dpb.vif_type, dpb.ip_address, dpb.window_column FROM SecurityGroupBoundPorts sgp JOIN DownPortBindings dpb ON sgp.port_id = dpb.port_id WHERE sgp.security_group_binding_count >= 1 ORDER BY sgp.security_group_binding_count DESC, sgp.dns_record_count DESC, dpb.ip_address) SELECT i.tenant_id AS qualifying_ports_tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT i.port_id) AS total_qualifying_ports, avg_q.avg_qualifying_port_count FROM inner_cte i JOIN ( SELECT AVG(tenant_port_count) AS avg_qualifying_port_count FROM ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT port_id) AS tenant_port_count FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ) AS per_tenant ) AS avg_q ON 1 = 1 GROUP BY i.tenant_id, avg_q.avg_qualifying_port_count ORDER BY total_qualifying_ports DESC, qualifying_ports_tenant_id;

question: For ports that are DOWN and are bound to host "drive-59", show each port’s ID, tenant ID, and MAC address, along with the two running-sum window metrics from the base query. Additionally, compute the average of the DOWN-ports running-sum metric across all returned ports as a benchmark, and classify each port as 'ABOVE_BENCHMARK' (at least 50% above the benchmark), 'BELOW_BENCHMARK' (at least 50% below the benchmark), or 'AROUND_BENCHMARK'.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH subq1 AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), subq2 AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, p.TENANT_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59' ) SELECT s2.PORT_ID AS port_id, s2.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, s2.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, s1.window_column AS down_ports_running_sum_by_resource_type, s2.window_column AS drive_59_ports_running_sum_by_vif_type FROM subq2 s2 JOIN subq1 s1 ON s1.port_id = s2.PORT_ID AND s1.tenant_id = s2.TENANT_ID AND s1.mac_address = s2.MAC_ADDRESS ORDER BY s2.PORT_ID ), benchmark_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(down_ports_running_sum_by_resource_type) AS avg_down_running_sum FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.down_ports_running_sum_by_resource_type, i.drive_59_ports_running_sum_by_vif_type, b.avg_down_running_sum AS benchmark, CASE WHEN i.down_ports_running_sum_by_resource_type > b.avg_down_running_sum * 1.5 THEN 'ABOVE_BENCHMARK' WHEN i.down_ports_running_sum_by_resource_type < b.avg_down_running_sum * 0.5 THEN 'BELOW_BENCHMARK' ELSE 'AROUND_BENCHMARK' END AS benchmark_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN benchmark_cte b ORDER BY i.port_id;

question: For each VIF type, report the VIF type, the number of DOWN ports, the average per-port windowed average admin_state_up (2 preceding and 2 following rows partitioned by VIF type and ordered by MAC address), and the average (across the involved hosts) variance of port standard attribute IDs for DOWN ports that have an IP allocation. Also include subtotals per VIF type and a grand total. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH DownPortsWindow AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ), HostStandardAttrVariance AS ( SELECT b.HOST, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND ia.PORT_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY b.HOST ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC ) SELECT dpw.VIF_TYPE, COUNT(*) AS down_ports_count, AVG(dpw.window_column) AS avg_window_admin_state_up, AVG(hsav.standard_attr_id_variance) AS avg_standard_attr_id_variance_across_hosts FROM DownPortsWindow dpw JOIN HostStandardAttrVariance hsav ON dpw.HOST = hsav.HOST GROUP BY dpw.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY down_ports_count DESC ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(inner_cte.VIF_TYPE) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE inner_cte.VIF_TYPE END AS VIF_TYPE, SUM(inner_cte.down_ports_count) AS down_ports_count, AVG(inner_cte.avg_window_admin_state_up) AS avg_window_admin_state_up, AVG(inner_cte.avg_standard_attr_id_variance_across_hosts) AS avg_standard_attr_id_variance_across_hosts FROM inner_cte GROUP BY inner_cte.VIF_TYPE WITH ROLLUP;

question: For ports that are DOWN and belong to ACTIVE networks, return the same port/network details as before (port ID, network ID, port name, MAC address, port admin_state_up, binding host, VIF type, the 2-preceding/2-following window average of port admin_state_up by VIF type ordered by MAC address; plus the active network’s name, tenant ID, network admin_state_up, MTU, the network standard attribute updated_at timestamp, and the row number of the network within its tenant ordered by network name). Then, only keep rows where the network’s MTU is greater than the average MTU across all ACTIVE networks. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH DownPortsWithBindings AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS), ActiveNetworksWithAttrs AS (SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE'), DownPortsOnActiveNetworks AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, dpb.NAME AS port_name, dpb.MAC_ADDRESS, dpb.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS port_admin_state_up, dpb.HOST AS binding_host, dpb.VIF_TYPE, dpb.window_column AS port_admin_state_up_avg_window_2_pre_2_fol, an.network_name, an.tenant_id, an.admin_state_up AS network_admin_state_up, an.mtu, an.standard_attr_updated_at, an.window_column AS network_row_number_within_tenant FROM PORTS p JOIN DownPortsWithBindings dpb ON p.MAC_ADDRESS = dpb.MAC_ADDRESS AND p.NAME = dpb.NAME AND p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = dpb.ADMIN_STATE_UP JOIN ActiveNetworksWithAttrs an ON an.network_id = p.NETWORK_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT * FROM DownPortsOnActiveNetworks ORDER BY tenant_id, network_id, MAC_ADDRESS ), ActiveNetworkMtuAvg AS ( SELECT AVG(n.MTU) AS avg_active_network_mtu FROM NETWORKS n WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' ) SELECT i.* FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN ActiveNetworkMtuAvg a WHERE i.mtu > a.avg_active_network_mtu ORDER BY i.tenant_id, i.network_id, i.MAC_ADDRESS;

question: For each tenant that has administratively up ports (admin_state_up = 1) bound to at least one security group, list the tenant ID, the total number of such ports, the average number of such ports across all tenants as a benchmark, and categorize the tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'. Only consider ports that also have at least one port security binding. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH SecurityGroupBoundPorts AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name ), PortSecurityBindingsSummary AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ), CombinedPortDetails AS ( SELECT sg.port_id, sg.tenant_id, sg.port_name, ps.mac_address, sg.security_group_binding_count, sg.dns_record_count, ps.binding_count AS port_security_binding_count, ps.port_security_enabled_total FROM SecurityGroupBoundPorts sg JOIN PortSecurityBindingsSummary ps ON sg.port_id = ps.port_id ) SELECT port_id, tenant_id, port_name, mac_address, security_group_binding_count, dns_record_count, port_security_binding_count, port_security_enabled_total FROM CombinedPortDetails ORDER BY tenant_id, port_id ), TenantQualifiedPorts AS ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT port_id) AS total_ports FROM inner_cte WHERE port_security_binding_count > 0 GROUP BY tenant_id ), AverageQualifiedPorts AS ( SELECT AVG(total_ports) AS avg_ports FROM TenantQualifiedPorts ) SELECT tqp.tenant_id, tqp.total_ports, aqp.avg_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN tqp.total_ports > aqp.avg_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN tqp.total_ports < aqp.avg_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category FROM TenantQualifiedPorts tqp CROSS JOIN AverageQualifiedPorts aqp;

question: For each tenant, find the tenant ID and the maximum number of security group bindings on any DOWN port (with admin_state_up = 1) for that tenant, considering only ports that have at least one security group binding, and also report the maximum total DNS records associated with any such port for that tenant. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH PortSecurityGroupAndDnsCounts AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name ), DownPortBindingRanks AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT dpr.port_id, dpr.port_name, psc.tenant_id, dpr.mac_address, dpr.binding_host, dpr.vif_type, dpr.window_column AS down_status_rank, psc.security_group_binding_count, psc.dns_record_count FROM DownPortBindingRanks dpr JOIN PortSecurityGroupAndDnsCounts psc ON dpr.port_id = psc.port_id ORDER BY psc.security_group_binding_count DESC, psc.dns_record_count DESC, dpr.port_id ) SELECT tenant_id, MAX(security_group_binding_count) AS max_security_group_bindings_on_a_down_port, MAX(dns_record_count) AS max_dns_records_on_a_down_port FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id;

question: For each of the top 3 networks with the most IPv4 subnets that are shared via RBAC entries with action = 'access_as_shared', list the network ID and subnet count, and include the IPv4 subnet details (subnet name, tenant ID, IP version, CIDR, gateway IP, DHCP enabled flag, allocation pool first/last IP), plus only those subnet rows whose max subnet standard attribute ID over the current subnet row and the next 2 rows (when ordered by subnet ID) is greater than the average of that same windowed max value across all returned subnets. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH subnet_details AS ( SELECT s.NAME, s.TENANT_ID, s.NETWORK_ID, s.IP_VERSION, s.CIDR, s.GATEWAY_IP, s.ENABLE_DHCP, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, MAX(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( ORDER BY s.ID ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS AS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ), top_shared_networks AS ( SELECT n.OBJECT_ID AS network_id, COUNT(*) AS subnet_count FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.OBJECT_ID ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 3 ) SELECT tsn.network_id, tsn.subnet_count, sd.NAME AS subnet_name, sd.TENANT_ID AS subnet_tenant_id, sd.IP_VERSION, sd.CIDR, sd.GATEWAY_IP, sd.ENABLE_DHCP, sd.FIRST_IP AS allocation_pool_first_ip, sd.LAST_IP AS allocation_pool_last_ip, sd.max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM top_shared_networks tsn JOIN subnet_details sd ON sd.NETWORK_ID = tsn.network_id ORDER BY tsn.subnet_count DESC, tsn.network_id, sd.NAME) SELECT i.network_id, i.subnet_count, i.subnet_name, i.subnet_tenant_id, i.IP_VERSION, i.CIDR, i.GATEWAY_IP, i.ENABLE_DHCP, i.allocation_pool_first_ip, i.allocation_pool_last_ip, i.max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM inner_cte i JOIN ( SELECT AVG(max_standard_attr_id_next2) AS avg_max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM inner_cte ) a ON 1 = 1 WHERE i.max_standard_attr_id_next2 > a.avg_max_standard_attr_id_next2 ORDER BY i.subnet_count DESC, i.network_id, i.subnet_name;

question: For each IPv4 subnet name whose DNS nameserver order range is greater than the average DNS nameserver order range across all IPv4 subnets, return the subnet name, the order range (max minus min), the variance of the DNS nameserver order values, and the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the DNS nameserver order values. Do not return any rounded answers.
