network_row_number_within_tenant, ap.PORT_ID, ap.HOST, ap.VIF_TYPE, ap.VNIC_TYPE, ap.MAC_ADDRESS, ap.STATUS AS port_status, ap.DEVICE_OWNER, ap.window_column AS avg_standard_attr_id_window_2_preceding_2_following FROM ActiveNetworks an JOIN AdminUpPorts ap ON ap.NETWORK_ID = an.network_id AND ap.TENANT_ID = an.tenant_id ), TenantActiveAdminUpPortCounts AS ( SELECT n.tenant_id, n.id AS network_id, COUNT(p.id) AS admin_up_port_count FROM NETWORKS n JOIN PORTS p ON p.network_id = n.id AND p.tenant_id = n.tenant_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' AND p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY n.tenant_id, n.id ), TenantActiveAdminUpAverages AS ( SELECT tenant_id, AVG(admin_up_port_count) AS avg_admin_up_ports_per_active_network FROM TenantActiveAdminUpPortCounts GROUP BY tenant_id ) SELECT i.network_id, i.network_name, i.tenant_id, i.admin_state_up, i.mtu, i.standard_attr_updated_at, i.network_row_number_within_tenant, i.port_id, i.host, i.vif_type, i.vnic_type, i.mac_address, i.port_status, i.device_owner, i.avg_standard_attr_id_window_2_preceding_2_following FROM inner_cte i JOIN TenantActiveAdminUpPortCounts c ON c.tenant_id = i.tenant_id AND c.network_id = i.network_id JOIN TenantActiveAdminUpAverages a ON a.tenant_id = i.tenant_id WHERE c.admin_up_port_count > a.avg_admin_up_ports_per_active_network;

question: Across tenants, compute how many administratively up ports meet the criteria of being bound to at least one security group, having at least one port security binding, and having more than 75% of their port security bindings enabled. Return each tenant’s ID, the number of such qualifying ports, the average qualifying-port count across all tenants as a benchmark, and label each tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% above average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% below average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH PortSecurityGroupDNS AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name ), PortSecurityBindings AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ) SELECT psgd.port_id, psgd.tenant_id, psgd.port_name, psb.mac_address, psgd.security_group_binding_count, psb.binding_count, psb.port_security_enabled_total, psgd.dns_record_count FROM PortSecurityGroupDNS psgd JOIN PortSecurityBindings psb ON psgd.port_id = psb.port_id WHERE (psb.port_security_enabled_total * 1.0 / psb.binding_count) > 0.75 ), TenantQualifyingPorts AS ( SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(port_id) AS qualifying_ports FROM inner_cte GROUP BY tenant_id ), AverageQualifyingPorts AS ( SELECT AVG(qualifying_ports) AS avg_qualifying_ports FROM TenantQualifyingPorts ) SELECT tqp.tenant_id, tqp.qualifying_ports, aqp.avg_qualifying_ports AS benchmark, CASE WHEN tqp.qualifying_ports > aqp.avg_qualifying_ports * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_USER' WHEN tqp.qualifying_ports < aqp.avg_qualifying_ports * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_USER' ELSE 'AVERAGE_USER' END AS user_category FROM TenantQualifyingPorts tqp CROSS JOIN AverageQualifyingPorts aqp;

question: For ports bound to the security group ID 0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c, list each port’s ID, status, allocated IP address, and the running sum of its standard attribute ID within its network (ordered by standard attribute ID), along with (for that same port status) the range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the number of port security bindings per port, and the total number of ports in that security group having that status; additionally, include the average number of ports per status within that security group as a benchmark and categorize each port’s status as HIGH_STATUS (at least 50% above the benchmark), LOW_STATUS (at least 50% below the benchmark), or AVERAGE_STATUS. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH PortDetailsForSecurityGroup AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.STATUS AS port_status, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c' ), PortSecurityBindingStatsByStatus AS ( SELECT p.status, MAX(ps.binding_count) - MIN(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_range, VARIANCE(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_variance, STDDEV(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_stddev FROM ports AS p JOIN ( SELECT p2.id AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS binding_count FROM ports AS p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings AS b ON p2.id = b.port_id GROUP BY p2.id ) AS ps ON p.id = ps.port_id GROUP BY p.status ORDER BY binding_count_range DESC ), SecurityGroupPortStatusCounts AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS ports_in_security_group FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID WHERE sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c' GROUP BY p.STATUS ) SELECT pd.port_id, pd.port_status, pd.ip_address, pd.window_column, pss.binding_count_range, pss.binding_count_variance, pss.binding_count_stddev, sgc.ports_in_security_group FROM PortDetailsForSecurityGroup pd JOIN PortSecurityBindingStatsByStatus pss ON pd.port_status = pss.status JOIN SecurityGroupPortStatusCounts sgc ON pd.port_status = sgc.port_status ORDER BY pd.port_status, pd.window_column, pd.port_id ), StatusBenchmark AS ( SELECT AVG(ports_in_security_group) AS avg_ports_per_status FROM ( SELECT port_status, MAX(ports_in_security_group) AS ports_in_security_group FROM inner_cte GROUP BY port_status ) s ) SELECT i.port_id, i.port_status, i.ip_address, i.window_column, i.binding_count_range, i.binding_count_variance, i.binding_count_stddev, i.ports_in_security_group, sb.avg_ports_per_status AS benchmark, CASE WHEN i.ports_in_security_group > sb.avg_ports_per_status * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_STATUS' WHEN i.ports_in_security_group < sb.avg_ports_per_status * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_STATUS' ELSE 'AVERAGE_STATUS' END AS status_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN StatusBenchmark sb ORDER BY i.port_status, i.window_column, i.port_id;

question: Among the top 10 tenants with the most ACTIVE networks, show each tenant’s ID, total number of ACTIVE networks, and whether the tenant has any IPv4 subnets whose route-count range is greater than 0 (based on per-subnet next-hop route counts). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH SubnetRouteStats AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(route_count) - MIN(route_count) AS route_count_range, VARIANCE(route_count) AS route_count_variance, STDDEV(route_count) AS route_count_stddev FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN ( SELECT sr.SUBNET_ID, COUNT(*) AS route_count FROM SUBNETROUTES AS sr GROUP BY sr.SUBNET_ID, sr.NEXTHOP ) AS route_stats ON s.ID = route_stats.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY route_count_range DESC ), ActiveNetworks AS ( SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' ) SELECT an.tenant_id, an.network_id, an.network_name, an.admin_state_up, an.mtu, an.standard_attr_updated_at, an.window_column, srs.subnet_name, srs.route_count_range, srs.route_count_variance, srs.route_count_stddev FROM ActiveNetworks an JOIN SUBNETS s ON s.NETWORK_ID = an.network_id AND s.IP_VERSION = 4 JOIN SubnetRouteStats srs ON srs.subnet_name = s.NAME) SELECT i.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT i.network_id) AS total_active_networks, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN i.route_count_range > 0 THEN i.subnet_name END) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_ipv4_subnet_with_nonzero_route_range FROM inner_cte i GROUP BY i.tenant_id ORDER BY total_active_networks DESC LIMIT 10;

question: For each tenant that has ports on host "drive-59", show the tenant ID, the number of distinct ports on that host, the number of those ports that are administratively up and have port security enabled (matched by MAC address), the secured-port ratio (secured ports divided by total drive-59 ports) rounded to 2 decimals, and also include the overall average secured-port ratio across all such tenants.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH HostDrive59Ports AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, p.TENANT_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59' ), AdminUpPorts AS ( SELECT p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED AS port_security_enabled, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 ), Drive59AdminUpSummary AS ( SELECT h.TENANT_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT h.PORT_ID) AS drive59_port_count, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a.port_security_enabled = 1 THEN h.PORT_ID END) AS drive59_secured_port_count, ROUND( COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a.port_security_enabled = 1 THEN h.PORT_ID END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT h.PORT_ID), 0), 2 ) AS secured_port_ratio FROM HostDrive59Ports h JOIN AdminUpPorts a ON a.mac_address = h.MAC_ADDRESS GROUP BY h.TENANT_ID ) SELECT s.TENANT_ID, s.drive59_port_count, s.drive59_secured_port_count, s.secured_port_ratio FROM Drive59AdminUpSummary s ORDER BY s.secured_port_ratio DESC, s.drive59_port_count DESC ) SELECT inner_cte.TENANT_ID, inner_cte.drive59_port_count, inner_cte.drive59_secured_port_count, inner_cte.secured_port_ratio, avg_stats.avg_secured_port_ratio FROM inner_cte JOIN ( SELECT AVG(secured_port_ratio) AS avg_secured_port_ratio FROM inner_cte ) AS avg_stats ON 1 = 1 ORDER BY inner_cte.secured_port_ratio DESC, inner_cte.drive59_port_count DESC;

question: For active networks with admin_state_up = 1 that have at least one DOWN port, return the tenant ID, network ID, network name, admin_state_up flag, MTU, the network’s standard attribute updated_at timestamp, and the count of DOWN ports—only for those networks whose DOWN-port count is greater than the average DOWN-port count among all active admin_state_up = 1 networks. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH DownPorts AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), ActiveNetworks AS ( SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' ) SELECT an.tenant_id, an.network_id, an.network_name, an.admin_state_up, an.mtu, an.standard_attr_updated_at, COUNT(DISTINCT dp.port_id) AS down_port_count FROM ActiveNetworks an LEFT JOIN DownPorts dp ON dp.network_id = an.network_id AND dp.tenant_id = an.tenant_id WHERE an.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY an.tenant_id, an.network_id, an.network_name, an.admin_state_up, an.mtu, an.standard_attr_updated_at HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT dp.port_id) > 0 ORDER BY down_port_count DESC, an.network_name ) , DownPortAverages AS ( SELECT AVG(down_port_count) AS avg_down_ports FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.tenant_id, i.network_id, i.network_name, i.admin_state_up, i.mtu, i.standard_attr_updated_at, i.down_port_count FROM inner_cte i WHERE i.down_port_count > (SELECT avg_down_ports FROM DownPortAverages) ORDER BY i.down_port_count DESC, i.network_name;

question: For each tenant that has ports on host "drive-59", show the tenant ID, the number of distinct ports on that host, the number of those ports that are administratively up and have port security enabled (matched by MAC address), the secured-port ratio (secured ports divided by total drive-59 ports) rounded to 2 decimals, and the deviation of that tenant’s secured-port ratio from the average secured-port ratio across all such tenants.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH HostDrive59Ports AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, p.TENANT_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59' ), AdminUpPorts AS ( SELECT p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED AS port_security_enabled, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 ), Drive59AdminUpSummary AS ( SELECT h.TENANT_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT h.PORT_ID) AS drive59_port_count, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a.port_security_enabled = 1 THEN h.PORT_ID END) AS drive59_secured_port_count, ROUND( COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a.port_security_enabled = 1 THEN h.PORT_ID END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT h.PORT_ID), 0), 2 ) AS secured_port_ratio FROM HostDrive59Ports h JOIN AdminUpPorts a ON a.mac_address = h.MAC_ADDRESS GROUP BY h.TENANT_ID ) SELECT s.TENANT_ID, s.drive59_port_count, s.drive59_secured_port_count, s.secured_port_ratio FROM Drive59AdminUpSummary s ORDER BY s.secured_port_ratio DESC, s.drive59_port_count DESC ), avg_cte AS ( SELECT AVG(secured_port_ratio) AS avg_secured_port_ratio FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.TENANT_ID, i.drive59_port_count, i.drive59_secured_port_count, i.secured_port_ratio, (i.secured_port_ratio - a.avg_secured_port_ratio) AS deviation_from_avg_secured_port_ratio FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_cte a ORDER BY deviation_from_avg_secured_port_ratio DESC, i.secured_port_ratio DESC, i.drive59_port_count DESC;

question: For each IPv4 subnet stats row (either DNS nameserver ORDER stats or per-next-hop route-count stats), list the subnet name, network ID, the stats fields, the “reason” label, and the deviation of that row’s range value from the average range among rows with the same reason. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH DnsOrderStats AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(d.ORDER) - MIN(d.ORDER) AS order_range, VARIANCE(d.ORDER) AS order_variance FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.id = d.subnet_id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY order_range DESC ), RouteCountStats AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(route_count) - MIN(route_count) AS route_count_range, VARIANCE(route_count) AS route_count_variance, STDDEV(route_count) AS route_count_stddev FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN ( SELECT sr.SUBNET_ID, COUNT(*) AS route_count FROM SUBNETROUTES AS sr GROUP BY sr.SUBNET_ID, sr.NEXTHOP ) AS route_stats ON s.ID = route_stats.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY route_count_range DESC ), CombinedSubnetStats AS ( SELECT subnet_name, order_range, order_variance, NULL AS route_count_range, NULL AS route_count_variance, NULL AS route_count_stddev, 'DNS Nameserver Order Stats' AS reason FROM DnsOrderStats UNION ALL SELECT subnet_name, NULL AS order_range, NULL AS order_variance, route_count_range, route_count_variance, route_count_stddev, 'Route Count Stats' AS reason FROM RouteCountStats ) SELECT * FROM CombinedSubnetStats ORDER BY subnet_name, reason) , Enriched AS ( SELECT i.subnet_name, s.network_id, i.order_range, i.order_variance, i.route_count_range, i.route_count_variance, i.route_count_stddev, i.reason, CASE WHEN i.reason = 'DNS Nameserver Order Stats' THEN i.order_range ELSE i.route_count_range END AS range_value FROM inner_cte i JOIN subnets s ON s.name = i.subnet_name AND s.ip_version = 4 ), AvgByReason AS ( SELECT reason, AVG(range_value) AS avg_range_value FROM Enriched GROUP BY reason ) SELECT e.subnet_name, e.network_id, e.order_range, e.order_variance, e.route_count_range, e.route_count_variance, e.route_count_stddev, e.reason, (e.range_value - a.avg_range_value) AS deviation_from_avg_range_within_reason FROM Enriched e JOIN AvgByReason a ON e.reason = a.reason ORDER BY e.subnet_name, e.reason;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN, list each port’s ID and tenant ID along with its binding host and VIF type, allocated IP address (with a row number ordered by IP address using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row), and the port’s MAC address with the running sum of standard attribute IDs within each resource type group ordered by standard attribute ID; additionally, for each tenant show the total number of distinct DOWN ports and the deviation of that tenant’s DOWN-port count from the average DOWN-port count across all tenants. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH DownPortBindingIPs AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), DownPortMacAttrSums AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT d1.port_id, d1.tenant_id, d1.host, d1.vif_type, d1.ip_address, d1.window_column AS ip_row_number_window, d2.mac_address, d2.window_column AS standard_attr_running_sum_window FROM DownPortBindingIPs d1 JOIN DownPortMacAttrSums d2 ON d1.port_id = d2.port_id ORDER BY d1.tenant_id, d1.port_id, d1.ip_address), TenantDownPortCounts AS (SELECT p.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS down_ports FROM PORTS p WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.tenant_id), AverageTenantDownPortCounts AS (SELECT AVG(down_ports) AS avg_down_ports FROM TenantDownPortCounts) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.host, i.vif_type, i.ip_address, i.ip_row_number_window, i.mac_address, i.standard_attr_running_sum_window, t.down_ports AS tenant_down_port_count, (t.down_ports - a.avg_down_ports) AS deviation_from_avg_tenant_down_port_count FROM inner_cte i JOIN TenantDownPortCounts t ON t.tenant_id = i.tenant_id CROSS JOIN AverageTenantDownPortCounts a ORDER BY i.tenant_id, i.port_id, i.ip_address;

question: From the top 10 tenants (among those with at least 2 DOWN ports) ranked by the number of distinct DOWN ports, show each tenant’s ID, the distinct DOWN port count, the average row-number window value computed by ordering allocated IP addresses (frame: 2 preceding to 1 following), the average dense-rank window value computed by ordering port-security settings (frame: 2 preceding to current row), and whether the tenant has any ports bound to a host (i.e., any ML2 port binding exists). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH PortSecurityWindow AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY psb.port_security_enabled ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM ports AS p JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN'), PortIpBindingWindow AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT pibw.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT pibw.port_id) AS down_port_count, AVG(pibw.window_column) AS avg_ip_row_number_window, AVG(psw.window_column) AS avg_port_security_dense_rank_window FROM PortIpBindingWindow pibw JOIN PortSecurityWindow psw ON pibw.port_id = psw.port_id WHERE pibw.tenant_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY pibw.tenant_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT pibw.port_id) >= 2 ORDER BY down_port_count DESC, pibw.tenant_id ) SELECT i.tenant_id, i.down_port_count, i.avg_ip_row_number_window, i.avg_port_security_dense_rank_window, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT b.port_id) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_any_port_binding FROM inner_cte i LEFT JOIN ports p ON p.tenant_id = i.tenant_id LEFT JOIN ml2_port_bindings b ON b.port_id = p.id GROUP BY i.tenant_id, i.down_port_count, i.avg_ip_row_number_window, i.avg_port_security_dense_rank_window ORDER BY i.down_port_count DESC, i.tenant_id LIMIT 10;

question: For ports that are DOWN, list each port’s ID, tenant ID, name, network ID, MAC address, admin state, status, device owner, and security group ID, along with (1) the rank of the port within its security group when ordered by port ID and (2) the minimum admin_state_up value over a window of 3 preceding and 1 following row ordered by port ID. Do not repeat the security group ID if it is the same as the previous row, and include a subtotal row per security group showing the total number of DOWN ports in that security group. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH subq1 AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' ), subq2 AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT subq1.port_id, subq1.tenant_id, subq2.name AS port_name, subq2.network_id, subq1.mac_address, subq2.admin_state_up, subq2.status, subq2.device_owner, subq1.security_group_id, subq1.window_column AS port_rank_within_security_group_by_port_id, subq2.window_column AS min_admin_state_up_in_3_preceding_1_following_by_port_id FROM subq1 JOIN subq2 ON subq1.security_group_id = subq2.security_group_id AND subq1.mac_address = subq2.mac_address ORDER BY subq1.security_group_id, subq1.window_column, subq1.port_id ) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(security_group_id) OVER (ORDER BY security_group_id_sort, port_rank_within_security_group_by_port_id, port_id) = security_group_id THEN NULL ELSE security_group_id END AS security_group_id, port_id, tenant_id, port_name, network_id, mac_address, admin_state_up, status, device_owner, port_rank_within_security_group_by_port_id, min_admin_state_up_in_3_preceding_1_following_by_port_id, down_ports_in_security_group FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(security_group_id) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE security_group_id END AS security_group_id_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(security_group_id) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE security_group_id END AS security_group_id, port_id, tenant_id, port_name, network_id, mac_address, admin_state_up, status, device_owner, port_rank_within_security_group_by_port_id, min_admin_state_up_in_3_preceding_1_following_by_port_id, COUNT(*) AS down_ports_in_security_group FROM inner_cte GROUP BY security_group_id, port_id, tenant_id, port_name, network_id, mac_address, admin_state_up, status, device_owner, port_rank_within_security_group_by_port_id, min_admin_state_up_in_3_preceding_1_following_by_port_id WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY security_group_id_sort, port_rank_within_security_group_by_port_id, port_id;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN, return only those ports whose rank within the DOWN status group (ordered by port ID) is greater than the average of those ranks across all DOWN ports; list the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, the running sum of standard attribute IDs within each standard attribute resource type (ordered by standard attribute ID), plus the port name, binding host, VIF type, and the port’s rank. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH DownPortsStdAttrWindow AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), DownPortsBindingRank AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT s.port_id, s.tenant_id, s.mac_address, s.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_ids_within_resource_type, b.port_name, b.binding_host, b.vif_type, b.window_column AS rank_within_down_status_by_port_id FROM DownPortsStdAttrWindow s JOIN DownPortsBindingRank b ON s.port_id = b.port_id AND s.mac_address = b.mac_address ) SELECT port_id, tenant_id, mac_address, running_sum_standard_attr_ids_within_resource_type, port_name, binding_host, vif_type, rank_within_down_status_by_port_id FROM inner_cte WHERE rank_within_down_status_by_port_id > (SELECT AVG(rank_within_down_status_by_port_id) FROM inner_cte);

question: For each network, using the combined list of administratively-up ports (including those with status DOWN) from the prior result set, find the network ID and the maximum of the per-port window metric (admin-up window average standard attribute ID for “Admin State Up” rows, or down-window average port ID for “Status DOWN” rows) observed among ports in that network. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH AdminUpPorts AS (SELECT b.PORT_ID, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, b.VNIC_TYPE, p.TENANT_ID, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1), DownPortsWithIPs AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ia.SUBNET_ID AS subnet_id, AVG(p.ID) OVER (PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS), CombinedPorts AS ( SELECT a.PORT_ID AS port_id, a.HOST, a.VIF_TYPE, a.VNIC_TYPE, a.TENANT_ID, a.NETWORK_ID, a.MAC_ADDRESS, a.STATUS, a.DEVICE_OWNER, a.window_column AS admin_up_window_avg_standard_attr_id, NULL AS port_name, NULL AS ip_address, NULL AS subnet_id, NULL AS down_window_avg_port_id, 'Admin State Up' AS reason FROM AdminUpPorts a UNION ALL SELECT d.port_id, NULL AS HOST, NULL AS VIF_TYPE, NULL AS VNIC_TYPE, p.TENANT_ID, p.NETWORK_ID, d.mac_address AS MAC_ADDRESS, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, NULL AS admin_up_window_avg_standard_attr_id, d.port_name, d.ip_address, d.subnet_id, d.window_column AS down_window_avg_port_id, 'Status DOWN' AS reason FROM DownPortsWithIPs d JOIN PORTS p ON p.ID = d.port_id WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 ) SELECT * FROM CombinedPorts ORDER BY port_id, reason) , NetworkPortWindowMetric AS ( SELECT p.network_id, p.id AS port_id, MAX( COALESCE(inner_cte.admin_up_window_avg_standard_attr_id, inner_cte.down_window_avg_port_id) ) AS port_window_metric FROM inner_cte JOIN PORTS p ON p.id = inner_cte.port_id GROUP BY p.network_id, p.id ) SELECT network_id, MAX(port_window_metric) AS max_port_window_metric FROM NetworkPortWindowMetric GROUP BY network_id;

question: Among device owners that have DOWN ports bound to a security group, list the top 10 device owners by distinct DOWN port count, showing the device owner, distinct port count, minimum standard attribute ID, the variance of standard attribute IDs for DOWN ports that have an IP allocation, and the number of distinct networks those DOWN ports span. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH PortSecurityGroupStats AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), PortStatusStdAttrVariance AS ( SELECT p.STATUS, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM PORTS AS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.STATUS ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC ) SELECT psgs.port_status, psgs.device_owner, psgs.port_count, psgs.min_standard_attr_id, pssav.standard_attr_id_variance FROM PortSecurityGroupStats psgs JOIN PortStatusStdAttrVariance pssav ON psgs.port_status = pssav.STATUS ORDER BY psgs.port_status, psgs.device_owner ) SELECT i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.min_standard_attr_id, i.standard_attr_id_variance, COUNT(DISTINCT p.NETWORK_ID) AS distinct_networks FROM inner_cte i JOIN PORTS p ON p.DEVICE_OWNER = i.device_owner AND p.STATUS = i.port_status JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID GROUP BY i.device_owner, i.port_count, i.min_standard_attr_id, i.standard_attr_id_variance ORDER BY i.port_count DESC LIMIT 10;

question: For each network that has at least one DOWN port bound to a security group, find the network ID and the maximum (across its ports) of the per-port row number computed by ordering allocated IP addresses with a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row, using the DOWN-port details and status/device-owner security-group summary as the inner result. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH port_status_owner_sg_summary AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), down_ports_with_ip_window AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT d.port_id, d.tenant_id, d.host, d.vif_type, d.ip_address, d.window_column, s.port_status, s.device_owner, s.port_count, s.min_standard_attr_id FROM down_ports_with_ip_window d JOIN PORTS p ON p.ID = d.port_id JOIN port_status_owner_sg_summary s ON s.port_status = p.STATUS AND s.device_owner = p.DEVICE_OWNER) SELECT p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, MAX(i.window_column) AS max_ip_row_number FROM inner_cte i JOIN PORTS p ON p.ID = i.port_id JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON spb.PORT_ID = p.ID GROUP BY p.NETWORK_ID;

question: For DOWN ports that are bound to a security group, show the same per-device-owner and VIF-type statistics as before, but also include subtotals per device owner and a grand total. Do not repeat the device owner label when it is the same as the previous row. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH PortStatusOwnerStats AS (SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER), DownPortWindowDetails AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS), VifTypePortCounts AS ( SELECT b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS down_ports_with_sg_count FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY b.VIF_TYPE ) SELECT psos.port_status, psos.device_owner, psos.port_count, psos.min_standard_attr_id, dpwd.VIF_TYPE, vpc.down_ports_with_sg_count, AVG(dpwd.window_column) AS avg_window_admin_state_up_for_vif_type FROM PortStatusOwnerStats psos JOIN PORTS p ON p.STATUS = psos.port_status AND p.DEVICE_OWNER = psos.device_owner JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON spb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN DownPortWindowDetails dpwd ON dpwd.MAC_ADDRESS = p.MAC_ADDRESS JOIN VifTypePortCounts vpc ON vpc.vif_type = dpwd.VIF_TYPE GROUP BY psos.port_status, psos.device_owner, psos.port_count, psos.min_standard_attr_id, dpwd.VIF_TYPE, vpc.down_ports_with_sg_count ORDER BY psos.port_count DESC, dpwd.VIF_TYPE) SELECT CASE WHEN LAG(device_owner) OVER (ORDER BY device_owner_sort, device_owner, vif_type) = device_owner THEN NULL ELSE device_owner END AS device_owner, port_status, vif_type, port_count, min_standard_attr_id, down_ports_with_sg_count, avg_window_admin_state_up_for_vif_type FROM ( SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(device_owner) = 1 THEN 'zzz' ELSE device_owner END AS device_owner_sort, CASE WHEN GROUPING(device_owner) = 1 THEN 'TOTAL' ELSE device_owner END AS device_owner, port_status, vif_type, SUM(port_count) AS port_count, MIN(min_standard_attr_id) AS min_standard_attr_id, MAX(down_ports_with_sg_count) AS down_ports_with_sg_count, AVG(avg_window_admin_state_up_for_vif_type) AS avg_window_admin_state_up_for_vif_type FROM inner_cte GROUP BY device_owner, port_status, vif_type WITH ROLLUP ) AS tbltmp ORDER BY device_owner_sort, device_owner, vif_type;

question: For DOWN ports that have an IP allocation, show rollups of how many such ports exist per binding host and VIF type. Include subtotals per host and a grand total, while also reporting the maximum variance of the port standard attribute ID observed for each host within the same DOWN+allocated-IP set. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH DownPortsWithWindow AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), HostStandardAttrVariance AS ( SELECT b.HOST, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND ia.PORT_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY b.HOST ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC ) SELECT dpw.port_id, dpw.tenant_id, dpw.host, dpw.vif_type, dpw.ip_address, dpw.window_column, hsv.standard_attr_id_variance FROM DownPortsWithWindow dpw JOIN HostStandardAttrVariance hsv ON dpw.host = hsv.HOST ORDER BY hsv.standard_attr_id_variance DESC, dpw.ip_address ), HostVifCounts AS ( SELECT i.host, i.vif_type, COUNT(DISTINCT i.port_id) AS total_ports, MAX(i.standard_attr_id_variance) AS host_standard_attr_id_variance FROM inner_cte i GROUP BY i.host, i.vif_type ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(host) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE host END AS host, CASE WHEN GROUPING(vif_type) = 1 AND GROUPING(host) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' WHEN GROUPING(vif_type) = 1 AND GROUPING(host) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE vif_type END AS vif_type, SUM(total_ports) AS total_ports, MAX(host_standard_attr_id_variance) AS host_standard_attr_id_variance FROM HostVifCounts GROUP BY host, vif_type WITH ROLLUP;

question: For IPv4 subnets, using the detailed subnet-and-route listing as a base, summarize how many result rows fall under each DHCP enabled flag and route presence category (label as 'Has Routes' when a subnet has at least one associated route row, otherwise 'No Routes'). Include subtotals per DHCP flag and a grand total. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH SubnetDetails AS (SELECT s.NAME, s.TENANT_ID, s.NETWORK_ID, s.IP_VERSION, s.CIDR, s.GATEWAY_IP, s.ENABLE_DHCP, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, MAX(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( ORDER BY s.ID ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS AS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4), SubnetRouteDetails AS (SELECT r.DESTINATION, r.NEXTHOP, s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.SUBNET_ID ORDER BY r.SUBNET_ID) AS window_column FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4) SELECT sd.NAME AS subnet_name, sd.TENANT_ID, sd.NETWORK_ID, sd.IP_VERSION, sd.CIDR, sd.GATEWAY_IP, sd.ENABLE_DHCP, sd.FIRST_IP AS allocation_first_ip, sd.LAST_IP AS allocation_last_ip, sd.max_standard_attr_id_next2, srd.DESTINATION AS route_destination, srd.NEXTHOP AS route_nexthop, srd.window_column AS route_dense_rank_within_subnet FROM SubnetDetails sd LEFT JOIN SubnetRouteDetails srd ON sd.NAME = srd.subnet_name AND sd.CIDR = srd.subnet_cidr AND sd.FIRST_IP = srd.FIRST_IP AND sd.LAST_IP = srd.LAST_IP ORDER BY sd.NAME, srd.window_column, srd.DESTINATION), RoutePresenceSummary AS (SELECT ic.ENABLE_DHCP, CASE WHEN ic.route_destination IS NOT NULL THEN 'Has Routes' ELSE 'No Routes' END AS route_presence, COUNT(*) AS total_rows FROM inner_cte ic GROUP BY ic.ENABLE_DHCP, route_presence) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(ENABLE_DHCP) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE CAST(ENABLE_DHCP AS CHAR) END AS enable_dhcp, CASE WHEN GROUPING(route_presence) = 1 AND GROUPING(ENABLE_DHCP) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE route_presence END AS route_presence, SUM(total_rows) AS total_rows FROM RoutePresenceSummary GROUP BY ENABLE_DHCP, route_presence WITH ROLLUP;

question: For active networks, list each tenant’s networks (with a row number per tenant ordered by network name) and, for the ports on those networks whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports', show the port status and device owner along with the number of ports and the earliest standard-attribute updated timestamp for that status/owner; additionally, return only those rows where the port_count is greater than the average port_count for the same port_status across all status/owner groups. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH PortStatusOwnerStats AS (SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER), ActiveTenantNetworks AS (SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE'), ActiveTenantPortStatusOwnerStats AS ( SELECT atn.tenant_id, atn.network_id, atn.network_name, atn.admin_state_up, atn.mtu, atn.standard_attr_updated_at, atn.window_column, psos.port_status, psos.device_owner, psos.port_count, psos.earliest_standard_attr_update FROM ActiveTenantNetworks atn JOIN PORTS p ON p.NETWORK_ID = atn.network_id JOIN PortStatusOwnerStats psos ON psos.port_status = p.STATUS AND psos.device_owner = p.DEVICE_OWNER JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa_p ON sa_p.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa_p.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY atn.tenant_id, atn.network_id, atn.network_name, atn.admin_state_up, atn.mtu, atn.standard_attr_updated_at, atn.window_column, psos.port_status, psos.device_owner, psos.port_count, psos.earliest_standard_attr_update ) SELECT * FROM ActiveTenantPortStatusOwnerStats ORDER BY tenant_id, window_column, network_id, port_status, device_owner) , StatusAverages AS ( SELECT port_status, AVG(port_count) AS avg_port_count FROM ( SELECT psos.port_status, psos.device_owner, psos.port_count FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID JOIN ( SELECT p2.STATUS AS port_status, p2.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p2.ID) AS port_count FROM PORTS p2 JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa2 ON sa2.ID = p2.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa2.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p2.STATUS, p2.DEVICE_OWNER ) psos ON psos.port_status = p.STATUS AND psos.device_owner = p.DEVICE_OWNER WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY psos.port_status, psos.device_owner, psos.port_count ) grouped_counts GROUP BY port_status ) SELECT i.* FROM inner_cte i JOIN StatusAverages sa ON sa.port_status = i.port_status WHERE i.port_count > sa.avg_port_count ORDER BY i.tenant_id, i.window_column, i.network_id, i.port_status, i.device_owner;

question: For IPv4 subnets whose routes have next hop 10.30.19.197/8, list each subnet route’s destination and next hop along with the subnet name and CIDR and the allocation pool’s first and last IP (including a dense rank per subnet), and also show the subnet-level range and variance of allocation pool starting IPs (FIRST_IP) for that subnet; additionally, compute the average FIRST_IP range across these subnets as a benchmark and categorize each subnet as 'HIGH_SPREAD' (at least 50% above average), 'LOW_SPREAD' (at least 50% below average), or 'AVERAGE_SPREAD'. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH FirstIpStatsBySubnet AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(p.FIRST_IP) - MIN(p.FIRST_IP) AS first_ip_range, VARIANCE(p.FIRST_IP) AS first_ip_variance FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE r.NEXTHOP = '10.30.19.197/8' GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY first_ip_range DESC ), SubnetRoutePoolDetails AS ( SELECT r.DESTINATION, r.NEXTHOP, s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.SUBNET_ID ORDER BY r.SUBNET_ID) AS window_column FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ), CombinedSubnetResults AS ( SELECT d.subnet_name, d.subnet_cidr, d.DESTINATION, d.NEXTHOP, d.FIRST_IP, d.LAST_IP, d.window_column, s.first_ip_range, s.first_ip_variance FROM SubnetRoutePoolDetails d JOIN FirstIpStatsBySubnet s ON d.subnet_name = s.subnet_name WHERE d.NEXTHOP = '10.30.19.197/8' ) SELECT * FROM CombinedSubnetResults ORDER BY subnet_name, DESTINATION, FIRST_IP), AvgFirstIpRange AS (SELECT AVG(first_ip_range) AS avg_first_ip_range FROM inner_cte) SELECT i.subnet_name, i.subnet_cidr, i.DESTINATION, i.NEXTHOP, i.FIRST_IP, i.LAST_IP, i.window_column, i.first_ip_range, i.first_ip_variance, a.avg_first_ip_range AS benchmark, CASE WHEN i.first_ip_range > a.avg_first_ip_range * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_SPREAD' WHEN i.first_ip_range < a.avg_first_ip_range * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_SPREAD' ELSE 'AVERAGE_SPREAD' END AS spread_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN AvgFirstIpRange a ORDER BY i.subnet_name, i.DESTINATION, i.FIRST_IP;

question: For each binding host, find the host name and the highest total number of times port security is enabled across any single port on that host—considering only ports that are DOWN but administratively up, and only including ports where port security is enabled at least once. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH DownPortsWithBindings AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), AdminUpPortSecurityStats AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address) SELECT d.port_id, d.port_name, d.mac_address, d.binding_host, d.vif_type, d.window_column, a.tenant_id, a.binding_count, a.port_security_enabled_total FROM DownPortsWithBindings d JOIN AdminUpPortSecurityStats a ON d.port_id = a.port_id WHERE a.port_security_enabled_total > 0 ORDER BY a.port_security_enabled_total DESC, d.port_id), HostPortSecurity AS ( SELECT binding_host, port_id, MAX(port_security_enabled_total) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM inner_cte GROUP BY binding_host, port_id ) SELECT binding_host, MAX(port_security_enabled_total) AS max_port_security_enabled_total FROM HostPortSecurity GROUP BY binding_host;

question: For IPv4 subnets that belong to networks with an RBAC action of 'access_as_shared', group results by the RBAC target tenant and DHCP enabled flag, and list the RBAC target tenant, DHCP flag, the number of distinct subnets, and the average of the per-subnet max-to-running-sum ratio (rounded to 2 decimals). Include subtotals per RBAC target tenant and a grand total.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH Subq1 AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, n.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant, SUM(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY s.IP_VERSION ORDER BY s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' ), Subq2 AS ( SELECT s.NAME, s.TENANT_ID, s.NETWORK_ID, s.IP_VERSION, s.CIDR, s.GATEWAY_IP, s.ENABLE_DHCP, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, MAX(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( ORDER BY s.ID ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS AS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ) SELECT q2.NAME AS subnet_name, q2.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, q2.TENANT_ID AS subnet_tenant_id, q2.NETWORK_ID AS subnet_network_id, q2.IP_VERSION AS ip_version, q2.GATEWAY_IP AS gateway_ip, q2.ENABLE_DHCP AS enable_dhcp, q2.FIRST_IP AS allocation_pool_first_ip, q2.LAST_IP AS allocation_pool_last_ip, q1.rbac_target_tenant, q1.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_ip_version, q2.max_standard_attr_id_next2, ROUND(q2.max_standard_attr_id_next2 / NULLIF(q1.window_column, 0), 2) AS max_to_running_sum_ratio FROM Subq2 q2 JOIN Subq1 q1 ON q1.subnet_name = q2.NAME AND q1.subnet_cidr = q2.CIDR ORDER BY max_to_running_sum_ratio DESC ) , Agg AS ( SELECT rbac_target_tenant, enable_dhcp, COUNT(DISTINCT subnet_name) AS distinct_subnets, ROUND(AVG(max_to_running_sum_ratio), 2) AS avg_max_to_running_sum_ratio FROM inner_cte GROUP BY rbac_target_tenant, enable_dhcp ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(rbac_target_tenant) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE rbac_target_tenant END AS rbac_target_tenant, CASE WHEN GROUPING(enable_dhcp) = 1 AND GROUPING(rbac_target_tenant) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' WHEN GROUPING(enable_dhcp) = 1 AND GROUPING(rbac_target_tenant) = 1 THEN 'ALL' ELSE CAST(enable_dhcp AS CHAR) END AS enable_dhcp, SUM(distinct_subnets) AS distinct_subnets, ROUND(AVG(avg_max_to_running_sum_ratio), 2) AS avg_max_to_running_sum_ratio FROM Agg GROUP BY rbac_target_tenant, enable_dhcp WITH ROLLUP;

question: For ports with status = 'DOWN', return only those ports whose standard attribute ID is greater than the average standard attribute ID among all DOWN ports with the same VIF type. For each such port, list the port ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, the row number ordered by IP address using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row, the port’s MAC address, and the running sum of standard attribute IDs within each resource type group ordered by standard attribute ID. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH DownPortBindingsAndIPs AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), DownPortsMacAndStdAttrRunningSum AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT d1.port_id, d1.tenant_id, d1.host, d1.vif_type, d1.ip_address, d1.window_column AS ip_row_number_window, d2.mac_address, d2.window_column AS stdattr_id_running_sum_window FROM DownPortBindingsAndIPs d1 JOIN DownPortsMacAndStdAttrRunningSum d2 ON d1.port_id = d2.port_id AND d1.tenant_id = d2.tenant_id ), VifTypeAverages AS ( SELECT b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, AVG(sa.ID) AS avg_stdattr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY b.VIF_TYPE ) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.host, i.vif_type, i.ip_address, i.ip_row_number_window, i.mac_address, i.stdattr_id_running_sum_window FROM inner_cte i JOIN PORTS p ON p.ID = i.port_id JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.ID > (SELECT v.avg_stdattr_id FROM VifTypeAverages v WHERE v.vif_type = i.vif_type);

question: For ACTIVE networks, find those that have an RBAC action of 'access_as_shared' and match them to subnets whose network is also shared to the same RBAC target tenant. Return the network name, status, admin_state_up, RBAC action and target tenant, along with the subnet name and CIDR, the running sum of subnet standard attribute IDs within each IP version group (ordered by standard attribute ID), and the dense rank within each network. Additionally, include the network standard attribute ID and filter to only rows where the subnet running-sum is greater than 50,000. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH SharedSubnets AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, n.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant, SUM(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY s.IP_VERSION ORDER BY s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' ), ActiveNetworkRBACs AS ( SELECT n.name, n.status, n.admin_state_up, r.action, r.target_tenant, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY n.id ORDER BY n.id) AS window_column FROM networksecuritybindings b JOIN networks n ON b.network_id = n.id JOIN networkrbacs r ON n.id = r.object_id WHERE n.status = 'ACTIVE' ) SELECT anr.name AS network_name, anr.status AS network_status, anr.admin_state_up, anr.action AS rbac_action, anr.target_tenant AS rbac_target_tenant, ss.subnet_name, ss.subnet_cidr, ss.window_column AS subnet_std_attr_running_sum_by_ip_version, anr.window_column AS network_dense_rank_within_network FROM ActiveNetworkRBACs anr JOIN SharedSubnets ss ON ss.rbac_target_tenant = anr.target_tenant AND anr.action = 'access_as_shared' ORDER BY anr.name, ss.subnet_name) SELECT i.network_name, i.network_status, i.admin_state_up, i.rbac_action, i.rbac_target_tenant, i.subnet_name, i.subnet_cidr, i.subnet_std_attr_running_sum_by_ip_version, i.network_dense_rank_within_network, n.standard_attr_id AS network_standard_attr_id FROM inner_cte i JOIN networks n ON n.name = i.network_name WHERE i.subnet_std_attr_running_sum_by_ip_version > 50000 ORDER BY i.network_name, i.subnet_name;

question: Return the same combined list as before (default external networks plus port-count summary rows), and for every row also show the deviation of its metric_value from the overall average metric_value across the entire combined result set. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH PortStatusOwnerStats AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), DefaultExternalNetworks AS ( SELECT e.NETWORK_ID, n.NAME, n.STATUS, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP, AVG(n.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER (PARTITION BY n.STATUS ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM EXTERNALNETWORKS e JOIN NETWORKS n ON e.NETWORK_ID = n.ID WHERE e.IS_DEFAULT = 0 ), CombinedResults AS ( SELECT den.NETWORK_ID AS entity_id, den.NAME AS entity_name, den.STATUS AS status, den.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, den.window_column AS metric_value, 'Default External Network' AS record_type FROM DefaultExternalNetworks den UNION ALL SELECT NULL AS entity_id, NULL AS entity_name, psos.port_status AS status, NULL AS admin_state_up, psos.port_count AS metric_value, 'Port Count by Status/Owner (ports resource_type)' AS record_type FROM PortStatusOwnerStats psos ) SELECT record_type, entity_id, entity_name, status, admin_state_up, metric_value FROM CombinedResults ORDER BY record_type, status, entity_name, entity_id), avg_metrics AS ( SELECT AVG(metric_value) AS avg_metric_value FROM inner_cte ) SELECT i.record_type, i.entity_id, i.entity_name, i.status, i.admin_state_up, i.metric_value, (i.metric_value - a.avg_metric_value) AS deviation_from_overall_avg_metric_value FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN avg_metrics a ORDER BY i.record_type, i.status, i.entity_name, i.entity_id;

question: For the port with ID `25d421c1-c76d-4c26-9550-9f871a1d5034`, group the results by the port’s security group ID and whether the port is administratively up (`Admin Up` vs `Admin Down`). For each group, show the security group ID, the admin-up label, the number of allowed address pairs, the number of distinct allowed address pair IP addresses, and the total port-security-enabled count across bindings. Include subtotals per security group and a grand total. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH allowed_address_pairs_details AS ( SELECT aap.MAC_ADDRESS AS allowed_mac_address, aap.IP_ADDRESS AS allowed_ip_address, p.ID AS port_id, sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID AS security_group_id, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY aap.IP_ADDRESS ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN ALLOWEDADDRESSPAIRS AS aap ON p.ID = aap.PORT_ID WHERE p.ID = '25d421c1-c76d-4c26-9550-9f871a1d5034' ORDER BY aap.IP_ADDRESS ), admin_up_port_security_summary AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ) SELECT aapd.allowed_mac_address, aapd.allowed_ip_address, aapd.port_id, aapd.security_group_id, aapd.window_column, apSS.tenant_id, apSS.mac_address AS port_mac_address, apSS.binding_count, apSS.port_security_enabled_total FROM allowed_address_pairs_details aapd JOIN admin_up_port_security_summary apSS ON aapd.port_id = apSS.port_id ), PortAdminStatus AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, CASE WHEN p.admin_state_up = 1 THEN 'Admin Up' ELSE 'Admin Down' END AS admin_status FROM ports p ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(i.security_group_id) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE i.security_group_id END AS security_group_id, CASE WHEN GROUPING(pas.admin_status) = 1 AND GROUPING(i.security_group_id) = 0 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' WHEN GROUPING(pas.admin_status) = 1 AND GROUPING(i.security_group_id) = 1 THEN 'SUBTOTAL' ELSE pas.admin_status END AS admin_status, COUNT(*) AS allowed_address_pairs_count, COUNT(DISTINCT i.allowed_ip_address) AS distinct_allowed_ip_count, SUM(COALESCE(i.port_security_enabled_total, 0)) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM inner_cte i JOIN PortAdminStatus pas ON pas.port_id = i.port_id GROUP BY i.security_group_id, pas.admin_status WITH ROLLUP;

question: For the RBAC action access_as_shared, show the action together with (1) the variance of subnet IP version (IPv4 vs IPv6) across subnets on the referenced networks, and (2) the overall average, range (max minus min), and variance of subnet IP version (considering only subnets with IP version 4 or 6) for networks referenced by RBAC entries with that same action; additionally, include whether any of those referenced networks have at least one IPv6 subnet (Yes/No). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH RbacSharedIpVersionVariance AS (SELECT n.ACTION, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_variance DESC), RbacIpVersionStats AS (SELECT n.ACTION AS rbac_action, AVG(s.IP_VERSION) AS avg_ip_version, MAX(s.IP_VERSION) - MIN(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_range, VARIANCE(s.IP_VERSION) AS ip_version_variance FROM NETWORKRBACS AS n JOIN SUBNETS AS s ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION IN (4, 6) GROUP BY n.ACTION ORDER BY ip_version_range DESC) SELECT rs.ACTION AS rbac_action, rs.ip_version_variance AS shared_action_ip_version_variance, ris.avg_ip_version, ris.ip_version_range, ris.ip_version_variance AS overall_ip_version_variance FROM RbacSharedIpVersionVariance rs JOIN RbacIpVersionStats ris ON rs.ACTION = ris.rbac_action ORDER BY rs.ip_version_variance DESC) SELECT i.rbac_action, i.shared_action_ip_version_variance, i.avg_ip_version, i.ip_version_range, i.overall_ip_version_variance, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN s2.IP_VERSION = 6 THEN s2.ID END) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_any_ipv6_subnet_on_referenced_networks FROM inner_cte i JOIN NETWORKRBACS n2 ON n2.ACTION = i.rbac_action JOIN SUBNETS s2 ON s2.NETWORK_ID = n2.OBJECT_ID GROUP BY i.rbac_action, i.shared_action_ip_version_variance, i.avg_ip_version, i.ip_version_range, i.overall_ip_version_variance ORDER BY i.shared_action_ip_version_variance DESC;

question: For ports that are DOWN, list the port name, network ID, MAC address, admin state, status, device owner, the bound security group ID, and the minimum admin_state_up value in a window of 3 preceding and 1 following row ordered by port ID, along with (for the DOWN status) the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) (standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) divided by average) of the length of allocated IP address strings for ports that have port security enabled; additionally, for each returned DOWN port, include the number of allocated IP addresses on that port and the deviation of that count from the average allocated-IP count across all DOWN ports in the result. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH PortStatusIPLenCV AS (SELECT p.status, STDDEV(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) / NULLIF(AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM portsecuritybindings psb JOIN ports p ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON p.id = ia.port_id WHERE psb.port_security_enabled = 1 GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC), DownPortsWithSecurityGroup AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT d.NAME, d.NETWORK_ID, d.MAC_ADDRESS, d.ADMIN_STATE_UP, d.STATUS, d.DEVICE_OWNER, d.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, d.window_column, cv.coefficient_of_variation AS status_ip_length_coefficient_of_variation FROM DownPortsWithSecurityGroup d JOIN PortStatusIPLenCV cv ON d.STATUS = cv.status ORDER BY cv.coefficient_of_variation DESC, d.NAME), DownPortIpCounts AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, COUNT(DISTINCT ia.ip_address) AS allocated_ip_count FROM ports p JOIN inner_cte i ON p.name = i.name AND p.network_id = i.network_id AND p.mac_address = i.mac_address AND p.admin_state_up = i.admin_state_up AND p.status = i.status AND p.device_owner = i.device_owner LEFT JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id GROUP BY p.id ), AvgDownPortIpCounts AS ( SELECT AVG(allocated_ip_count) AS avg_allocated_ip_count FROM DownPortIpCounts ) SELECT i.NAME, i.NETWORK_ID, i.MAC_ADDRESS, i.ADMIN_STATE_UP, i.STATUS, i.DEVICE_OWNER, i.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, i.window_column, i.status_ip_length_coefficient_of_variation, dpc.allocated_ip_count, (dpc.allocated_ip_count - adpc.avg_allocated_ip_count) AS deviation_from_avg_allocated_ip_count FROM inner_cte i JOIN ports p ON p.name = i.name AND p.network_id = i.network_id AND p.mac_address = i.mac_address AND p.admin_state_up = i.admin_state_up AND p.status = i.status AND p.device_owner = i.device_owner JOIN DownPortIpCounts dpc ON dpc.port_id = p.id CROSS JOIN AvgDownPortIpCounts adpc ORDER BY i.status_ip_length_coefficient_of_variation DESC, i.NAME;

question: Using the per-port details for administratively up ports that have at least one IP allocation (port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, port name, port security enabled status, the window row number ordered by MAC address with a frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row, the number of IP allocations, and the number of rows with a non-null subnet ID), compute the average IP allocation count across all returned ports as a benchmark and classify each port as 'HIGH_IP_ALLOC' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_IP_ALLOC' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_IP_ALLOC'. Return all original columns plus the benchmark and category. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH PortIpAllocSummary AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(ia.ip_address) AS ip_allocation_count, SUM(CASE WHEN ia.subnet_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS subnet_id_rows FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND ia.ip_address IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address), PortSecurityWindow AS (SELECT p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED AS port_security_enabled, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1), CombinedPortDetails AS ( SELECT s.port_id, s.tenant_id, s.mac_address, w.port_name, w.port_security_enabled, w.window_column, s.ip_allocation_count, s.subnet_id_rows FROM PortIpAllocSummary s JOIN PortSecurityWindow w ON w.mac_address = s.mac_address ) SELECT * FROM CombinedPortDetails ORDER BY tenant_id, mac_address, port_id), AvgIpAlloc AS (SELECT AVG(ip_allocation_count) AS avg_ip_allocation_count FROM inner_cte) SELECT i.port_id, i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.port_name, i.port_security_enabled, i.window_column, i.ip_allocation_count, i.subnet_id_rows, a.avg_ip_allocation_count AS benchmark, CASE WHEN i.ip_allocation_count > a.avg_ip_allocation_count * 1.5 THEN 'HIGH_IP_ALLOC' WHEN i.ip_allocation_count < a.avg_ip_allocation_count * 0.5 THEN 'LOW_IP_ALLOC' ELSE 'AVERAGE_IP_ALLOC' END AS ip_alloc_category FROM inner_cte i CROSS JOIN AvgIpAlloc a ORDER BY i.tenant_id, i.mac_address, i.port_id;

question: For each IPv4 subnet that has at least one DNS nameserver entry, show the subnet name, tenant ID, network ID, IP version, CIDR, gateway IP, DHCP enabled flag, allocation pool first IP and last IP, the maximum subnet standard attribute ID over the current subnet and the next 2 subnets by subnet ID, and also (per network) the maximum pool-count range across subnet names in that network, ordered by that network-level maximum range descending. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH SubnetPoolStatsByName AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(pool_count) - MIN(pool_count) AS pool_count_range, VARIANCE(pool_count) AS pool_count_variance, STDDEV(pool_count) AS pool_count_stddev FROM subnets AS s JOIN dnsnameservers AS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id JOIN ( SELECT s2.id AS subnet_id, COUNT(*) AS pool_count FROM subnets AS s2 JOIN ipallocationpools AS p ON p.subnet_id = s2.id GROUP BY s2.id, p.id ) AS pool_stats ON pool_stats.subnet_id = s.id GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY pool_count_range DESC ), SubnetDetailsWithWindowMax AS ( SELECT s.NAME, s.TENANT_ID, s.NETWORK_ID, s.IP_VERSION, s.CIDR, s.GATEWAY_IP, s.ENABLE_DHCP, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, MAX(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( ORDER BY s.ID ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS AS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ), DnsSubnetNames AS ( SELECT DISTINCT s.name AS subnet_name FROM subnets s JOIN dnsnameservers d ON d.subnet_id = s.id ) SELECT sd.NAME AS subnet_name, sd.TENANT_ID, sd.NETWORK_ID, sd.IP_VERSION, sd.CIDR, sd.GATEWAY_IP, sd.ENABLE_DHCP, sd.FIRST_IP, sd.LAST_IP, sd.max_standard_attr_id_next2, sp.pool_count_range, sp.pool_count_variance, sp.pool_count_stddev FROM SubnetDetailsWithWindowMax sd JOIN SubnetPoolStatsByName sp ON sd.NAME = sp.subnet_name JOIN DnsSubnetNames dn ON sd.NAME = dn.subnet_name ORDER BY sp.pool_count_range DESC, sd.NAME ), NetworkMaxPoolRange AS ( SELECT s.network_id, MAX(ic.pool_count_range) AS max_pool_count_range_in_network FROM inner_cte ic JOIN subnets s ON s.name = ic.subnet_name GROUP BY s.network_id ) SELECT ic.subnet_name, ic.tenant_id, ic.network_id, ic.ip_version, ic.cidr, ic.gateway_ip, ic.enable_dhcp, ic.first_ip, ic.last_ip, ic.max_standard_attr_id_next2, ic.pool_count_range, ic.pool_count_variance, ic.pool_count_stddev, nmr.max_pool_count_range_in_network FROM inner_cte ic JOIN NetworkMaxPoolRange nmr ON nmr.network_id = ic.network_id ORDER BY nmr.max_pool_count_range_in_network DESC, ic.pool_count_range DESC, ic.subnet_name;

question: For IPv4 subnets that belong to networks with an RBAC action of 'access_as_shared', return only those subnets whose max-to-running-sum ratio (maximum subnet standard attribute ID over the current row and next 2 rows, divided by the running sum of subnet standard attribute IDs within the IP version group, rounded to 2 decimals) is greater than the average of that same ratio across all such subnets; list the subnet’s name and CIDR along with its tenant ID, network ID, gateway IP, DHCP enabled flag, allocation pool first/last IP, the RBAC target tenant, the running sum, the max-over-next-2 value, and the ratio.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH Subq1 AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, n.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant, SUM(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY s.IP_VERSION ORDER BY s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' ), Subq2 AS ( SELECT s.NAME, s.TENANT_ID, s.NETWORK_ID, s.IP_VERSION, s.CIDR, s.GATEWAY_IP, s.ENABLE_DHCP, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, MAX(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( ORDER BY s.ID ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS AS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ) SELECT q2.NAME AS subnet_name, q2.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, q2.TENANT_ID AS subnet_tenant_id, q2.NETWORK_ID AS subnet_network_id, q2.IP_VERSION AS ip_version, q2.GATEWAY_IP AS gateway_ip, q2.ENABLE_DHCP AS enable_dhcp, q2.FIRST_IP AS allocation_pool_first_ip, q2.LAST_IP AS allocation_pool_last_ip, q1.rbac_target_tenant, q1.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_ip_version, q2.max_standard_attr_id_next2, ROUND(q2.max_standard_attr_id_next2 / NULLIF(q1.window_column, 0), 2) AS max_to_running_sum_ratio FROM Subq2 q2 JOIN Subq1 q1 ON q1.subnet_name = q2.NAME AND q1.subnet_cidr = q2.CIDR ORDER BY max_to_running_sum_ratio DESC ) SELECT subnet_name, subnet_cidr, subnet_tenant_id, subnet_network_id, ip_version, gateway_ip, enable_dhcp, allocation_pool_first_ip, allocation_pool_last_ip, rbac_target_tenant, running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_ip_version, max_standard_attr_id_next2, max_to_running_sum_ratio FROM inner_cte WHERE max_to_running_sum_ratio > (SELECT AVG(max_to_running_sum_ratio) FROM inner_cte) ORDER BY max_to_running_sum_ratio DESC;

question: For IPv4 subnets that have both subnet routes and DNS nameservers with a positive average nameserver order, show the route-count range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) (based on routes per next hop) and the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of DNS nameserver order values, and also include subtotals and a grand total across all qualifying subnets, ordered by the route-count range descending. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH q1 AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(route_count) - MIN(route_count) AS route_count_range, VARIANCE(route_count) AS route_count_variance, STDDEV(route_count) AS route_count_stddev FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN ( SELECT sr.SUBNET_ID, COUNT(*) AS route_count FROM SUBNETROUTES AS sr GROUP BY sr.SUBNET_ID, sr.NEXTHOP ) AS route_stats ON s.ID = route_stats.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY route_count_range DESC ), q2 AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, STDDEV(d.ORDER) / NULLIF(AVG(d.ORDER), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM subnets AS s JOIN dnsnameservers AS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id JOIN ipallocationpools AS p ON p.subnet_id = s.id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name HAVING AVG(d.ORDER) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ) SELECT q1.subnet_name, q1.route_count_range, q1.route_count_variance, q1.route_count_stddev, q2.coefficient_of_variation FROM q1 JOIN q2 ON q1.subnet_name = q2.subnet_name ORDER BY q1.route_count_range DESC ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(inner_cte.subnet_name) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE inner_cte.subnet_name END AS subnet_name, SUM(inner_cte.route_count_range) AS route_count_range, AVG(inner_cte.route_count_variance) AS route_count_variance, AVG(inner_cte.route_count_stddev) AS route_count_stddev, AVG(inner_cte.coefficient_of_variation) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte GROUP BY inner_cte.subnet_name WITH ROLLUP ORDER BY CASE WHEN GROUPING(inner_cte.subnet_name) = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, route_count_range DESC;

question: Using the DOWN-port details query as an inner CTE, list the top 10 tenants with the most DOWN ports. For each of these tenants, show the tenant ID, total number of DOWN ports, and whether any of their DOWN ports have an ML2 port binding with VIF type 'ovs'. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH DownPortStandardAttrWindow AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), DownPortBindingRank AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT dpsaw.port_id, dpsaw.tenant_id, dpbr.port_name, dpsaw.mac_address, dpbr.binding_host, dpbr.vif_type, dpsaw.window_column AS standard_attr_id_running_sum_within_resource_type, dpbr.window_column AS port_rank_within_down_status FROM DownPortStandardAttrWindow dpsaw JOIN DownPortBindingRank dpbr ON dpsaw.port_id = dpbr.port_id AND dpsaw.mac_address = dpbr.mac_address ORDER BY dpsaw.port_id ) SELECT i.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT i.port_id) AS total_down_ports, CASE WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN i.vif_type = 'ovs' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_ovs_vif_type_on_any_down_port FROM inner_cte i GROUP BY i.tenant_id ORDER BY total_down_ports DESC LIMIT 10;

question: Using the DOWN-port result set from the existing query as an inner CTE, for each VIF type return the VIF type and the maximum number of distinct device owners observed among DOWN ports in that VIF type (where device owners come from the port-status/device-owner aggregation and VIF types come from the windowed DOWN-port set). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH PortStatusOwnerAgg AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), DownPortsWindow AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ) SELECT psa.port_status, psa.device_owner, psa.port_count, psa.min_standard_attr_id, dpw.VIF_TYPE, COUNT(*) AS down_ports_in_vif_type, AVG(dpw.window_column) AS avg_window_admin_state_up FROM PortStatusOwnerAgg psa CROSS JOIN DownPortsWindow dpw GROUP BY psa.port_status, psa.device_owner, psa.port_count, psa.min_standard_attr_id, dpw.VIF_TYPE) SELECT VIF_TYPE, MAX(distinct_device_owners) AS max_distinct_device_owners FROM (SELECT VIF_TYPE, COUNT(DISTINCT device_owner) AS distinct_device_owners FROM inner_cte GROUP BY VIF_TYPE) t GROUP BY VIF_TYPE;

question: Using the same counts of distinct tenants with ACTIVE networks and distinct tenants with ports bound to host "drive-59", categorize the result by whether the ACTIVE network is admin-up ("Admin Up") or admin-down ("Admin Down"). Return the admin state category, the two tenant counts, and include subtotals and a grand total. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS ( WITH active_networks AS ( SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' ), drive59_ports AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, p.TENANT_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59' ) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT an.tenant_id) AS tenants_with_active_networks, COUNT(DISTINCT dp.tenant_id) AS tenants_with_ports_on_drive59 FROM active_networks an CROSS JOIN drive59_ports dp ) , AdminStateCounts AS ( SELECT CASE WHEN an.admin_state_up = 1 THEN 'Admin Up' ELSE 'Admin Down' END AS admin_state_category, COUNT(DISTINCT an.tenant_id) AS tenants_with_active_networks, COUNT(DISTINCT dp.tenant_id) AS tenants_with_ports_on_drive59 FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID JOIN ( SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' ) an ON an.network_id = n.ID CROSS JOIN ( SELECT p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59' ) dp GROUP BY admin_state_category ) SELECT CASE WHEN GROUPING(admin_state_category) = 1 THEN 'GRAND TOTAL' ELSE admin_state_category END AS admin_state_category, SUM(tenants_with_active_networks) AS tenants_with_active_networks, SUM(tenants_with_ports_on_drive59) AS tenants_with_ports_on_drive59 FROM AdminStateCounts GROUP BY admin_state_category WITH ROLLUP;

question: For each port status that appears in both result sets, return the port status along with (1) the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of ports’ standard attribute IDs for ports that have both a security group port binding and a port security binding, and (2) the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the allocated IP address string lengths for ports with port security enabled; additionally, only keep statuses where more than 75% of the distinct ports in that status have at least one IP allocation. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH inner_cte AS (WITH StdAttrIdCV_ByStatus AS ( SELECT p.status, STDDEV(p.standard_attr_id) / NULLIF(AVG(p.standard_attr_id), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM securitygroupportbindings AS sgpb JOIN ports AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(p.standard_attr_id) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ), IpAddressLenCV_ByStatus AS ( SELECT p.status, STDDEV(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) / NULLIF(AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM portsecuritybindings psb JOIN ports p ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON p.id = ia.port_id WHERE psb.port_security_enabled = 1 GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ) SELECT s1.status, s1.coefficient_of_variation AS std_attr_id_coefficient_of_variation, s2.coefficient_of_variation AS ip_address_length_coefficient_of_variation FROM StdAttrIdCV_ByStatus s1 JOIN IpAddressLenCV_ByStatus s2 ON s1.status = s2.status) SELECT i.status, i.std_attr_id_coefficient_of_variation, i.ip_address_length_coefficient_of_variation FROM inner_cte i JOIN ports p ON p.status = i.status LEFT JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id GROUP BY i.status, i.std_attr_id_coefficient_of_variation, i.ip_address_length_coefficient_of_variation HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN ia.ip_address IS NOT NULL THEN p.id END) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT p.id), 0) > 0.75;

question: For ports with status DOWN, list each port’s ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and its row number ordered by IP address (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row). Also include the corresponding summary for that port’s status and device owner considering only ports bound to a security group (distinct port count and minimum standard attribute ID), and add the average of these per-(status, device owner) port counts across all such DOWN groups. Do not return any rounded answers.
