SQL: WITH HaprxoyLBCountsByOpStatus AS ( SELECT lb.OPERATING_STATUS, COUNT(*) AS total_loadbalancers FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE pra.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy' GROUP BY lb.OPERATING_STATUS HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ), ActiveLBBytesInByOpStatus AS ( SELECT lb.OPERATING_STATUS, SUM(s.BYTES_IN) AS total_bytes_in FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS s ON lb.ID = s.LOADBALANCER_ID WHERE lb.PROVISIONING_STATUS = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY lb.OPERATING_STATUS HAVING SUM(s.BYTES_IN) > 1000000 ) SELECT h.OPERATING_STATUS, h.total_loadbalancers, a.total_bytes_in FROM HaprxoyLBCountsByOpStatus h JOIN ActiveLBBytesInByOpStatus a ON h.OPERATING_STATUS = a.OPERATING_STATUS ORDER BY a.total_bytes_in DESC;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN, return each port’s ID and tenant ID along with its binding host and VIF type, allocated IP address (with a row number ordered by IP address using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row), and also the port’s MAC address with the running sum of standard attribute IDs within each resource type group ordered by standard attribute ID. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH DownPortBindingIPs AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), DownPortMacAttrSums AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT d1.port_id, d1.tenant_id, d1.host, d1.vif_type, d1.ip_address, d1.window_column AS ip_row_number_window, d2.mac_address, d2.window_column AS standard_attr_running_sum_window FROM DownPortBindingIPs d1 JOIN DownPortMacAttrSums d2 ON d1.port_id = d2.port_id ORDER BY d1.tenant_id, d1.port_id, d1.ip_address;

question: List the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, and the running-sum window column for all ports that are either DOWN or on host "drive-59", along with a reason indicating whether the row came from the DOWN-ports-by-security-group calculation or the drive-59-ports-by-VIF-type calculation. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH DownPortsBySecurityGroup AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), Drive59PortsByVifType AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, p.TENANT_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59' ), CombinedPorts AS ( SELECT port_id, tenant_id, mac_address, window_column, 'DOWN (by Security Group)' AS reason FROM DownPortsBySecurityGroup UNION ALL SELECT PORT_ID AS port_id, TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, window_column, 'Host drive-59 (by VIF Type)' AS reason FROM Drive59PortsByVifType ) SELECT port_id, tenant_id, mac_address, window_column, reason FROM CombinedPorts ORDER BY tenant_id, port_id;

question: For each VIF type, show the VIF type, the number of DOWN ports, the average of the per-port windowed average admin_state_up (2 preceding and 2 following rows partitioned by VIF type and ordered by MAC address), and the average (across the involved hosts) variance of port standard attribute IDs for DOWN ports that have an IP allocation. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH DownPortsWindow AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ), HostStandardAttrVariance AS ( SELECT b.HOST, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND ia.PORT_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY b.HOST ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC ) SELECT dpw.VIF_TYPE, COUNT(*) AS down_ports_count, AVG(dpw.window_column) AS avg_window_admin_state_up, AVG(hsav.standard_attr_id_variance) AS avg_standard_attr_id_variance_across_hosts FROM DownPortsWindow dpw JOIN HostStandardAttrVariance hsav ON dpw.HOST = hsav.HOST GROUP BY dpw.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY down_ports_count DESC;

question: Find load balancers associated with the provider named 'haproxy' whose highest admin_state_up value is 1, and for each such load balancer return its name and operating status along with the total incoming bytes for that operating status across ACTIVE-provisioning load balancers, keeping only operating statuses where the total incoming bytes exceed 1,000,000. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH ActiveStatusBytes AS ( SELECT lb.OPERATING_STATUS, SUM(s.BYTES_IN) AS total_bytes_in FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS s ON lb.ID = s.LOADBALANCER_ID WHERE lb.PROVISIONING_STATUS = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY lb.OPERATING_STATUS HAVING SUM(s.BYTES_IN) > 1000000 ), HaproxyAdminUpLoadBalancers AS ( SELECT lb.name AS loadbalancer_name, MAX(lb.admin_state_up) AS max_admin_state_up, lb.operating_status FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS lb JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS pra ON lb.id = pra.resource_id WHERE pra.provider_name = 'haproxy' GROUP BY lb.name, lb.operating_status HAVING MAX(lb.admin_state_up) = 1 ) SELECT h.loadbalancer_name, h.operating_status, a.total_bytes_in FROM HaproxyAdminUpLoadBalancers h JOIN ActiveStatusBytes a ON h.operating_status = a.OPERATING_STATUS ORDER BY h.operating_status, h.loadbalancer_name;

question: For each port status (considering only administratively up ports), what is the count of administratively up ports and the range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the number of port security bindings per port (considering only ports that have at least one port security binding)? Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH administratively_up_ports AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, b.VNIC_TYPE, p.TENANT_ID, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 ), port_status_binding_stats AS ( SELECT p.status, MAX(ps.binding_count) - MIN(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_range, VARIANCE(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_variance, STDDEV(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_stddev FROM ports AS p JOIN ( SELECT p2.id AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS binding_count FROM ports AS p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings AS b ON p2.id = b.port_id GROUP BY p2.id ) AS ps ON p.id = ps.port_id GROUP BY p.status ORDER BY binding_count_range DESC ), up_port_counts_by_status AS ( SELECT aup.STATUS, COUNT(*) AS administratively_up_port_count FROM administratively_up_ports aup GROUP BY aup.STATUS ) SELECT psbs.status, ucs.administratively_up_port_count, psbs.binding_count_range, psbs.binding_count_variance, psbs.binding_count_stddev FROM port_status_binding_stats psbs JOIN up_port_counts_by_status ucs ON psbs.status = ucs.STATUS ORDER BY psbs.binding_count_range DESC;

question: For each VIF type among ports that are DOWN, show the VIF type, total number of distinct DOWN ports, the average of the MAC-address-based admin_state_up window metric, the maximum IP-address-based row-number window value, and the number of distinct tenants, by combining the DOWN-port MAC window results with the DOWN-port IP allocation row-number results joined on host and VIF type. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH PortDownMacWindow AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ), PortDownIpRowNumber AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT p2.vif_type, COUNT(DISTINCT p2.port_id) AS Total_Down_Ports, AVG(p1.window_column) AS Avg_AdminStateUp_Window_Across_Ports, MAX(p2.window_column) AS Max_Ip_RowNumber_Window, COUNT(DISTINCT p2.tenant_id) AS Distinct_Tenants FROM PortDownIpRowNumber p2 JOIN PortDownMacWindow p1 ON p1.HOST = p2.host AND p1.VIF_TYPE = p2.vif_type GROUP BY p2.vif_type ORDER BY Total_Down_Ports DESC;

question: For DOWN ports, list the tenant ID, the tenant’s total number of DOWN ports and average admin_state_up (rounded), along with each port’s security group ID and rank within that security group (by port ID), plus the port name, MAC address, admin_state_up flag, binding host, VIF type, the 2-preceding-to-2-following VIF-type window average of admin_state_up (ordered by MAC address), and the normalized ratio of that window average to the tenant’s average admin_state_up for DOWN ports.
SQL: WITH PortBindingsWindow AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, AVG(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ), SecurityGroupPortRank AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' ), TenantDownPortSummary AS ( SELECT p.tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS down_port_count, AVG(p.admin_state_up) AS avg_admin_state_up_down FROM PORTS p WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.tenant_id ) SELECT sgpr.tenant_id, tds.down_port_count, ROUND(tds.avg_admin_state_up_down, 2) AS avg_admin_state_up_down, sgpr.security_group_id, sgpr.port_id, pbw.NAME AS port_name, sgpr.mac_address, pbw.ADMIN_STATE_UP, pbw.HOST AS binding_host, pbw.VIF_TYPE, pbw.window_column AS avg_admin_state_up_viftype_mac_window, sgpr.window_column AS port_rank_within_security_group, ROUND( pbw.window_column / NULLIF(tds.avg_admin_state_up_down, 0), 2 ) AS normalized_viftype_window_vs_tenant_avg FROM SecurityGroupPortRank sgpr JOIN PortBindingsWindow pbw ON pbw.MAC_ADDRESS = sgpr.mac_address JOIN TenantDownPortSummary tds ON tds.tenant_id = sgpr.tenant_id ORDER BY normalized_viftype_window_vs_tenant_avg DESC, sgpr.security_group_id, sgpr.port_id;

question: For each network status, show the variance and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED across networks with at least one security binding, along with the total number of ports (restricted to standard attributes where RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports') for that same status; also list, for the matching port status, each device owner’s port count and the earliest standard attribute UPDATED_AT timestamp. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH NetworkSecurityStats AS ( SELECT n.STATUS AS network_status, VARIANCE(nsb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED) AS port_security_enabled_variance, STDDEV(nsb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED) AS port_security_enabled_stddev FROM NETWORKS AS n JOIN NETWORKSECURITYBINDINGS AS nsb ON n.ID = nsb.NETWORK_ID GROUP BY n.STATUS ORDER BY port_security_enabled_variance DESC ), PortOwnerStats AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), NetworkPortCountsByStatus AS ( SELECT n.STATUS AS network_status, COUNT(p.ID) AS total_ports_in_status FROM NETWORKS n JOIN PORTS p ON p.NETWORK_ID = n.ID JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY n.STATUS ) SELECT nss.network_status, nss.port_security_enabled_variance, nss.port_security_enabled_stddev, npc.total_ports_in_status, pos.port_status, pos.device_owner, pos.port_count, pos.earliest_standard_attr_update FROM NetworkSecurityStats nss JOIN NetworkPortCountsByStatus npc ON nss.network_status = npc.network_status JOIN PortOwnerStats pos ON pos.port_status = nss.network_status ORDER BY npc.total_ports_in_status DESC, nss.port_security_enabled_variance DESC, pos.port_count DESC;

question: For subnet names that are IPv4 and belong to networks with an RBAC action of 'access_as_shared' (keeping only subnet name/gateway IP groups where the maximum IP version is greater than 3), list each subnet name and gateway IP along with the maximum IP version and the range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the number of routes per subnet. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH route_metrics AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(route_count) - MIN(route_count) AS route_count_range, VARIANCE(route_count) AS route_count_variance, STDDEV(route_count) AS route_count_stddev FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN ( SELECT sr.SUBNET_ID, COUNT(*) AS route_count FROM SUBNETROUTES AS sr GROUP BY sr.SUBNET_ID, sr.NEXTHOP ) AS route_stats ON s.ID = route_stats.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY route_count_range DESC ), shared_rbac_max_ip AS ( SELECT s.name, MAX(s.ip_version) AS max_ip_version, s.gateway_ip FROM NETWORKRBACS n JOIN SUBNETS s ON n.object_id = s.network_id WHERE n.action = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY s.name, s.gateway_ip HAVING MAX(s.ip_version) > 3 ) SELECT rm.subnet_name, srm.gateway_ip, srm.max_ip_version, rm.route_count_range, rm.route_count_variance, rm.route_count_stddev FROM route_metrics rm JOIN shared_rbac_max_ip srm ON rm.subnet_name = srm.name ORDER BY rm.route_count_range DESC;

question: For ports whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports', list each port status and device owner with the number of ports and the earliest standard attribute updated timestamp, and also include (per port status) the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of standard attribute IDs considering only ports that have both a security group port binding and a port security binding. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH PortStatusOwnerStats AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), PortStatusVariation AS ( SELECT p.status, STDDEV(p.standard_attr_id) / NULLIF(AVG(p.standard_attr_id), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM securitygroupportbindings AS sgpb JOIN ports AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(p.standard_attr_id) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC ), CombinedPortStatusMetrics AS ( SELECT psos.port_status AS port_status, psos.device_owner AS device_owner, psos.port_count AS port_count, psos.earliest_standard_attr_update AS earliest_standard_attr_update, psv.coefficient_of_variation AS coefficient_of_variation FROM PortStatusOwnerStats psos JOIN PortStatusVariation psv ON psos.port_status = psv.status ) SELECT port_status, device_owner, port_count, earliest_standard_attr_update, coefficient_of_variation FROM CombinedPortStatusMetrics ORDER BY port_status, device_owner;

question: For each port that is DOWN and also has admin_state_up = 1 with at least one security group binding, list the port ID, tenant ID, port name, network ID, MAC address, device owner, allocated IP address, the row number within its network (ordered by port ID), the number of security group bindings, the total number of DNS records, and the DNS-records-per-security-group-binding ratio rounded to 2 decimals.
SQL: WITH PortSecurityAndDNS AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.name AS port_name, COUNT(sgpb.security_group_id) AS security_group_binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pd.port_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS dns_record_count FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN PORTDNSES pd ON p.id = pd.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.name ), DownPortsWithIPs AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT d.port_id, d.tenant_id, d.port_name, d.network_id, d.mac_address, d.device_owner, d.ip_address, d.window_column, psd.security_group_binding_count, psd.dns_record_count, ROUND(psd.dns_record_count / NULLIF(psd.security_group_binding_count, 0), 2) AS dns_records_per_security_group_binding FROM DownPortsWithIPs d JOIN PortSecurityAndDNS psd ON psd.port_id = d.port_id ORDER BY dns_records_per_security_group_binding DESC, d.network_id, d.window_column;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN, list each port’s ID, name, MAC address, binding host, and VIF type, along with (1) the port’s rank within the DOWN status group ordered by port ID and (2) the dense rank of the port when ordering by its port-security setting (PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED) using a window frame of the current row and the 2 preceding rows. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH PortSecurityWindow AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY psb.port_security_enabled ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM ports AS p JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' ), PortBindingRank AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT pbr.port_id, pbr.port_name, pbr.mac_address, pbr.binding_host, pbr.vif_type, pbr.window_column AS rank_within_down_status_by_port_id, psw.window_column AS dense_rank_by_port_security_with_2_preceding_frame FROM PortBindingRank pbr JOIN PortSecurityWindow psw ON pbr.port_id = psw.port_id ORDER BY pbr.port_id;

question: For active networks, list (per tenant) the first network by name (row_number = 1) along with the subnet (by subnet name) on that network that has at least one DNS nameserver entry, and show the subnet’s IP allocation pool count range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) together with the network’s admin_state_up flag, MTU, and standard-attribute updated_at timestamp. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH SubnetPoolStats AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(pool_count) - MIN(pool_count) AS pool_count_range, VARIANCE(pool_count) AS pool_count_variance, STDDEV(pool_count) AS pool_count_stddev FROM subnets AS s JOIN dnsnameservers AS d ON d.subnet_id = s.id JOIN ( SELECT s2.id AS subnet_id, COUNT(*) AS pool_count FROM subnets AS s2 JOIN ipallocationpools AS p ON p.subnet_id = s2.id GROUP BY s2.id, p.id ) AS pool_stats ON pool_stats.subnet_id = s.id GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY pool_count_range DESC ), ActiveNetworks AS ( SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' ) SELECT an.tenant_id, an.network_id, an.network_name, an.admin_state_up, an.mtu, an.standard_attr_updated_at, an.window_column, sps.subnet_name, sps.pool_count_range, sps.pool_count_variance, sps.pool_count_stddev FROM ActiveNetworks an JOIN subnets s ON s.network_id = an.network_id JOIN SubnetPoolStats sps ON sps.subnet_name = s.name WHERE an.window_column = 1 ORDER BY sps.pool_count_range DESC, an.tenant_id, an.network_name;

question: For each tenant that has ACTIVE networks, list the tenant ID, the number of unique active networks, the latest standard-attributes updated_at timestamp among those networks, the total number of administratively up ports for that tenant, the number of unique MAC addresses among those admin-up ports, and the minimum and maximum MAC address observed across all administratively up ports. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH ActiveNetworks AS ( SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' ), AdminUpPorts AS ( SELECT p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED AS port_security_enabled, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 ), TenantPortStats AS ( SELECT p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS admin_up_port_count, COUNT(DISTINCT p.MAC_ADDRESS) AS unique_mac_count FROM PORTS p WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 GROUP BY p.TENANT_ID ) SELECT an.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT an.network_id) AS active_networks, MAX(an.standard_attr_updated_at) AS latest_network_standard_attr_updated_at, tps.admin_up_port_count, tps.unique_mac_count, MIN(aup.mac_address) AS min_admin_up_port_mac_address, MAX(aup.mac_address) AS max_admin_up_port_mac_address FROM ActiveNetworks an LEFT JOIN TenantPortStats tps ON tps.tenant_id = an.tenant_id LEFT JOIN AdminUpPorts aup ON 1 = 1 GROUP BY an.tenant_id, tps.admin_up_port_count, tps.unique_mac_count ORDER BY active_networks DESC, an.tenant_id;

question: For ports that are DOWN, list each port’s ID, tenant ID, port name, network ID, MAC address, device owner, allocated IP address, the row number within its network (ordered by port ID), the bound security group ID, and the minimum admin_state_up value over a window of 3 preceding and 1 following port (ordered by port ID). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH DownPortsWithIPs AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), DownPortsWithSecurityWindow AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT dpi.port_id, dpi.tenant_id, dpi.port_name, dpi.network_id, dpi.mac_address, dpi.device_owner, dpi.ip_address, dpi.window_column AS row_num_within_network, dpsw.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, dpsw.ADMIN_STATE_UP, dpsw.STATUS, dpsw.window_column AS min_admin_state_up_window FROM DownPortsWithIPs dpi JOIN DownPortsWithSecurityWindow dpsw ON dpi.network_id = dpsw.NETWORK_ID AND dpi.port_name = dpsw.NAME AND dpi.mac_address = dpsw.MAC_ADDRESS AND dpi.device_owner = dpsw.DEVICE_OWNER ORDER BY dpi.network_id, dpi.port_id;

question: For DOWN ports that are bound to a security group, what are the port status, device owner, number of distinct ports, and minimum standard attribute ID—and, in the same result, how many distinct binding hosts exist for DOWN ports and what is the maximum variance of port standard attribute IDs across hosts (considering only DOWN ports with an IP allocation)? Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH port_status_owner_sg AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS min_standard_attr_id FROM PORTS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS spb ON p.ID = spb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), host_standard_attr_variance AS ( SELECT b.HOST, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND ia.PORT_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY b.HOST ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC ), host_count AS ( SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT b.HOST) AS host_count FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT psos.port_status, psos.device_owner, psos.port_count, psos.min_standard_attr_id, hc.host_count, (SELECT MAX(hsav.standard_attr_id_variance) FROM host_standard_attr_variance hsav) AS max_standard_attr_id_variance_across_hosts FROM port_status_owner_sg psos CROSS JOIN host_count hc;

question: For subnets on networks shared via the RBAC action 'access_as_shared' and restricted to IPv4, return each subnet’s name, CIDR, RBAC target tenant, the running sum of subnet standard attribute IDs within its IP-version partition ordered by standard attribute ID, and the dense rank of its standard attribute ID ordered by the standard attribute updated-at timestamp (using a window frame of the current row and the 2 preceding rows). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH shared_subnets AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, n.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant, SUM(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY s.IP_VERSION ORDER BY s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' ), ipv4_dense_ranks AS ( SELECT s.NAME, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY sa.UPDATED_AT ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES AS sa ON sa.ID = s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ) SELECT ss.subnet_name, ss.subnet_cidr, ss.rbac_target_tenant, ss.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_ids_ipv_group, idr.window_column AS dense_rank_by_updated_at_ipv4 FROM shared_subnets ss JOIN ipv4_dense_ranks idr ON idr.NAME = ss.subnet_name;

question: List each IPv4 subnet name that either (a) has more than 5 DNS nameserver entries (showing the standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of its DNS nameserver order values) or (b) has a standard attribute (showing the dense rank of its standard attribute ID ordered by the standard attribute updated-at timestamp using a window of the current row and the 2 preceding rows), and include a label indicating which metric each row represents. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH DnsOrderStddevBySubnet AS ( SELECT s.name, STDDEV(d.ORDER) AS order_stddev FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.id = d.subnet_id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name HAVING COUNT(*) > 5 ORDER BY order_stddev DESC ), StandardAttrDenseRankBySubnet AS ( SELECT s.NAME, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY sa.UPDATED_AT ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES AS sa ON sa.ID = s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ), CombinedSubnetMetrics AS ( SELECT name, order_stddev AS metric_value, 'DNS Order Stddev' AS metric_type FROM DnsOrderStddevBySubnet UNION ALL SELECT NAME, window_column AS metric_value, 'Standard Attr Dense Rank' AS metric_type FROM StandardAttrDenseRankBySubnet ) SELECT * FROM CombinedSubnetMetrics ORDER BY name, metric_type;

question: For each subnet that belongs to a network with an RBAC action of 'access_as_shared' and has a maximum IP version greater than 3 (grouped by subnet name and gateway IP), list the subnet name, gateway IP, that maximum IP version, the IPv4 DNS nameserver order range and variance for the subnet name, and the normalized order range (order range divided by the maximum IP version), ordered by the normalized order range descending.
SQL: WITH SubnetDNSOrderStats AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(d.ORDER) - MIN(d.ORDER) AS order_range, VARIANCE(d.ORDER) AS order_variance FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.id = d.subnet_id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY order_range DESC ), SharedNetworkSubnetMaxIP AS ( SELECT s.name, MAX(s.ip_version) AS max_ip_version, s.gateway_ip FROM NETWORKRBACS n JOIN SUBNETS s ON n.object_id = s.network_id WHERE n.action = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY s.name, s.gateway_ip HAVING MAX(s.ip_version) > 3 ) SELECT sm.name AS subnet_name, sm.gateway_ip, sm.max_ip_version, sd.order_range, sd.order_variance, ROUND(sd.order_range / NULLIF(sm.max_ip_version, 0), 2) AS Order_Range_Per_Max_IP_Version FROM SharedNetworkSubnetMaxIP sm JOIN SubnetDNSOrderStats sd ON sd.subnet_name = sm.name ORDER BY Order_Range_Per_Max_IP_Version DESC;

question: For ports that are administratively up, have at least one IP allocation, and also have status DOWN, show the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, the number of IP allocations on the port, the total number of rows with a non-null subnet ID among those allocations, and the port’s dense-rank by its port-security setting using a window frame of the current row and the 2 preceding rows, ordered by the IP allocation count descending. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH sq1 AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(ia.ip_address) AS ip_allocation_count, SUM(CASE WHEN ia.subnet_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS subnet_id_rows FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND ia.ip_address IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ), sq2 AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY psb.port_security_enabled ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM ports AS p JOIN portsecuritybindings AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' ) SELECT sq1.port_id, sq1.tenant_id, sq1.mac_address, sq1.ip_allocation_count, sq1.subnet_id_rows, sq2.window_column FROM sq1 JOIN sq2 ON sq1.port_id = sq2.port_id ORDER BY sq1.ip_allocation_count DESC;

question: For haproxy load balancers that are in ACTIVE provisioning status, list the load balancer name, ID, VIP address, provisioning status, operating status, the running average of the load balancer ID within the haproxy provider group ordered by load balancer name, and the total incoming bytes for that operating status—keeping only operating statuses whose total incoming bytes (across ACTIVE load balancers) exceed 1,000,000. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH HapLoadBalancers AS (SELECT lb.NAME, lb.ID, lb.VIP_ADDRESS, lb.PROVISIONING_STATUS, lb.OPERATING_STATUS, AVG(lb.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY pra.PROVIDER_NAME ORDER BY lb.NAME ) AS window_column FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE pra.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy'), OperatingStatusBytesIn AS (SELECT lb.OPERATING_STATUS, SUM(s.BYTES_IN) AS total_bytes_in FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS s ON lb.ID = s.LOADBALANCER_ID WHERE lb.PROVISIONING_STATUS = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY lb.OPERATING_STATUS HAVING SUM(s.BYTES_IN) > 1000000) SELECT hlb.NAME, hlb.ID, hlb.VIP_ADDRESS, hlb.PROVISIONING_STATUS, hlb.OPERATING_STATUS, hlb.window_column, osbi.total_bytes_in FROM HapLoadBalancers hlb JOIN OperatingStatusBytesIn osbi ON hlb.OPERATING_STATUS = osbi.OPERATING_STATUS WHERE hlb.PROVISIONING_STATUS = 'ACTIVE' ORDER BY hlb.NAME;

question: From the top 10 networks with the most DOWN ports, list each network ID and its DOWN-port count, and for each DOWN port show the port ID, tenant ID, port name, MAC address, device owner, allocated IP address, binding host, VIF type, the port’s row number within its network (ordered by port ID), and the port’s rank within the DOWN status group (ordered by port ID). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH sq1 AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), sq2 AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), top_networks AS ( SELECT network_id, COUNT(DISTINCT port_id) AS down_port_count FROM sq2 GROUP BY network_id ORDER BY down_port_count DESC LIMIT 10 ) SELECT tn.network_id, tn.down_port_count, sq2.port_id, sq2.tenant_id, sq2.port_name, sq2.mac_address, sq2.device_owner, sq2.ip_address, sq2.window_column AS port_row_number_within_network, sq1.binding_host, sq1.vif_type, sq1.window_column AS port_rank_within_down_status FROM top_networks tn JOIN sq2 ON tn.network_id = sq2.network_id LEFT JOIN sq1 ON sq2.port_id = sq1.port_id ORDER BY tn.down_port_count DESC, tn.network_id, sq2.window_column, sq2.port_id;

question: Among ports whose status is DOWN and that have an IP allocation, list each such port’s name, network ID, MAC address, admin_state_up, status, device owner, bound security group ID, and the minimum admin_state_up over a window of 3 preceding and 1 following ports ordered by port ID; also include the port’s binding host and that host’s variance of port standard_attr_id. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH DownPortSecurityWindow AS ( SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), HostDownPortAttrVariance AS ( SELECT b.HOST, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND ia.PORT_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY b.HOST ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC ), DownPortsWithIpOnHosts AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, b.HOST FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON ia.PORT_ID = p.ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' AND ia.PORT_ID IS NOT NULL ) SELECT dpsw.NAME, dpsw.NETWORK_ID, dpsw.MAC_ADDRESS, dpsw.ADMIN_STATE_UP, dpsw.STATUS, dpsw.DEVICE_OWNER, dpsw.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, dpsw.window_column, hdpav.HOST, hdpav.standard_attr_id_variance FROM DownPortSecurityWindow dpsw JOIN PORTS p ON p.NAME = dpsw.NAME AND p.NETWORK_ID = dpsw.NETWORK_ID AND p.MAC_ADDRESS = dpsw.MAC_ADDRESS AND p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = dpsw.ADMIN_STATE_UP AND p.STATUS = dpsw.STATUS AND p.DEVICE_OWNER = dpsw.DEVICE_OWNER JOIN DownPortsWithIpOnHosts dpwh ON dpwh.port_id = p.ID JOIN HostDownPortAttrVariance hdpav ON hdpav.HOST = dpwh.HOST ORDER BY hdpav.standard_attr_id_variance DESC, dpsw.NETWORK_ID, dpsw.NAME;

question: For IPv4 subnets whose network has an RBAC action of 'access_as_shared', list each subnet’s name and CIDR, the RBAC target tenant, the running sum of subnet standard attribute IDs within the IPv4 group (ordered by standard attribute ID), and the range and variance of the DNS nameserver order values configured for that subnet. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH IPv4SubnetDNSOrderStats AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(d.ORDER) - MIN(d.ORDER) AS order_range, VARIANCE(d.ORDER) AS order_variance FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.id = d.subnet_id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY order_range DESC ), SharedNetworkSubnets AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, n.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant, SUM(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY s.IP_VERSION ORDER BY s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' ), SharedIPv4SubnetDNSAndRBACDetails AS ( SELECT sns.subnet_name, sns.subnet_cidr, sns.rbac_target_tenant, sns.window_column, ids.order_range, ids.order_variance FROM SharedNetworkSubnets sns JOIN IPv4SubnetDNSOrderStats ids ON ids.subnet_name = sns.subnet_name JOIN SUBNETS s ON s.NAME = sns.subnet_name WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ) SELECT * FROM SharedIPv4SubnetDNSAndRBACDetails ORDER BY subnet_name, rbac_target_tenant;

question: For ports on host "drive-59" that are administratively up, return the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, the running sum of the port standard attribute IDs within each VIF type group ordered by standard attribute ID, along with the number of port security bindings on the port and the total number of times port security is enabled across those bindings. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH PortWindowSums AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, p.TENANT_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59' ), AdminUpPortSecurityAgg AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ) SELECT pws.PORT_ID, pws.TENANT_ID, pws.MAC_ADDRESS, pws.window_column, aupsa.binding_count, aupsa.port_security_enabled_total FROM PortWindowSums pws JOIN AdminUpPortSecurityAgg aupsa ON pws.PORT_ID = aupsa.port_id AND pws.TENANT_ID = aupsa.tenant_id AND pws.MAC_ADDRESS = aupsa.mac_address;

question: For ports that are DOWN, show the port ID, port name, MAC address, binding host, VIF type, the port’s rank within the DOWN status group (ordered by port ID), and also the port security status and the admin-up row number (ordered by MAC address with a frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row), but only for those ports whose port security is enabled. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH DownPortsWithBindings AS (SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN'), AdminUpPortsWithSecurity AS (SELECT p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED AS port_security_enabled, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1) SELECT dpwb.port_id, dpwb.port_name, dpwb.mac_address, dpwb.binding_host, dpwb.vif_type, dpwb.window_column AS down_status_rank, aupws.port_security_enabled, aupws.window_column AS admin_up_row_number FROM DownPortsWithBindings dpwb JOIN AdminUpPortsWithSecurity aupws ON dpwb.mac_address = aupws.mac_address WHERE aupws.port_security_enabled = 1 ORDER BY dpwb.port_id;

question: For ACTIVE load balancers provided by the “haproxy” provider, list the load balancer name, ID, VIP address, provisioning status, operating status, the running average of the load balancer ID within the haproxy provider group ordered by load balancer name, the total incoming bytes for that operating status (only where total incoming bytes exceed 1,000,000), and the ratio of total incoming bytes to that running-average ID value.
SQL: WITH HapLoadBalancers AS (SELECT lb.NAME, lb.ID, lb.VIP_ADDRESS, lb.PROVISIONING_STATUS, lb.OPERATING_STATUS, AVG(lb.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY pra.PROVIDER_NAME ORDER BY lb.NAME ) AS window_column FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb JOIN PROVIDERRESOURCEASSOCIATIONS AS pra ON lb.ID = pra.RESOURCE_ID WHERE pra.PROVIDER_NAME = 'haproxy'), OperatingStatusBytesIn AS (SELECT lb.OPERATING_STATUS, SUM(s.BYTES_IN) AS total_bytes_in FROM LBAAS_LOADBALANCERS AS lb JOIN LBAAS_LOADBALANCER_STATISTICS AS s ON lb.ID = s.LOADBALANCER_ID WHERE lb.PROVISIONING_STATUS = 'ACTIVE' GROUP BY lb.OPERATING_STATUS HAVING SUM(s.BYTES_IN) > 1000000) SELECT hlb.NAME, hlb.ID, hlb.VIP_ADDRESS, hlb.PROVISIONING_STATUS, hlb.OPERATING_STATUS, hlb.window_column, osbi.total_bytes_in, ROUND(osbi.total_bytes_in / NULLIF(hlb.window_column, 0), 2) AS BytesIn_Per_WindowAvgId FROM HapLoadBalancers hlb JOIN OperatingStatusBytesIn osbi ON hlb.OPERATING_STATUS = osbi.OPERATING_STATUS WHERE hlb.PROVISIONING_STATUS = 'ACTIVE' ORDER BY BytesIn_Per_WindowAvgId DESC, hlb.NAME;

question: For ports on host "drive-59" that are administratively up and have at least one IP allocation, show the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, the number of IP allocations on the port, the total number of subnet-id rows among those allocations, and the running sum of port standard attribute IDs within each VIF type group ordered by standard attribute ID. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH PortIpAllocStats AS (SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(ia.ip_address) AS ip_allocation_count, SUM(CASE WHEN ia.subnet_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS subnet_id_rows FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND ia.ip_address IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address), HostVifWindowSums AS (SELECT b.PORT_ID, p.TENANT_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59') SELECT h.PORT_ID AS port_id, h.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, h.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, pias.ip_allocation_count, pias.subnet_id_rows, h.window_column FROM HostVifWindowSums h JOIN PortIpAllocStats pias ON pias.port_id = h.PORT_ID AND pias.tenant_id = h.TENANT_ID AND pias.mac_address = h.MAC_ADDRESS ORDER BY h.window_column DESC, h.PORT_ID;

question: For IPv4 subnets, list each subnet route’s destination and next hop along with the subnet name and CIDR and the allocation pool’s first and last IP, include a dense rank within each subnet, and also show (per subnet name) the range and variance of the DNS nameserver order values configured for that subnet. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH DnsOrderStats AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(d.ORDER) - MIN(d.ORDER) AS order_range, VARIANCE(d.ORDER) AS order_variance FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.id = d.subnet_id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY order_range DESC ), SubnetRoutePoolDetails AS ( SELECT r.DESTINATION, r.NEXTHOP, s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.SUBNET_ID ORDER BY r.SUBNET_ID) AS window_column FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ) SELECT srpd.subnet_name, srpd.subnet_cidr, srpd.DESTINATION, srpd.NEXTHOP, srpd.FIRST_IP, srpd.LAST_IP, srpd.window_column, dos.order_range, dos.order_variance FROM SubnetRoutePoolDetails srpd JOIN DnsOrderStats dos ON srpd.subnet_name = dos.subnet_name ORDER BY srpd.subnet_name, srpd.window_column, srpd.DESTINATION;

question: For ports that are DOWN (including their binding host, VIF type, and rank within the DOWN status group) and that also are administratively up with at least one IP allocation, list the port ID, port name, tenant ID, MAC address, binding host, VIF type, the number of IP allocations on the port, the total number of subnet-id rows from those allocations, and the port’s rank. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH AdminUpPortsWithIPs AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(ia.ip_address) AS ip_allocation_count, SUM(CASE WHEN ia.subnet_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS subnet_id_rows FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND ia.ip_address IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ), DownPortsWithBindings AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, b.HOST AS binding_host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.STATUS ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b ON p.ID = b.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT dpwb.port_id, dpwb.port_name, apwi.tenant_id, dpwb.mac_address, dpwb.binding_host, dpwb.vif_type, apwi.ip_allocation_count, apwi.subnet_id_rows, dpwb.window_column FROM DownPortsWithBindings dpwb JOIN AdminUpPortsWithIPs apwi ON dpwb.port_id = apwi.port_id ORDER BY dpwb.window_column, dpwb.port_id;

question: For each port that is administratively up, has at least one IP allocation, and is also in DOWN status, list the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, the number of IP allocations on that port, the number of rows with a non-null subnet ID among those allocations, the running sum of standard attribute IDs within each resource type group (ordered by standard attribute ID), and the ratio of IP allocation count to that running-sum value rounded to 2 decimals.
SQL: WITH AdminUpPortsWithIPs AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(ia.ip_address) AS ip_allocation_count, SUM(CASE WHEN ia.subnet_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS subnet_id_rows FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 AND ia.ip_address IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ), DownPortsWindow AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT a.port_id, a.tenant_id, a.mac_address, a.ip_allocation_count, a.subnet_id_rows, d.window_column, ROUND(a.ip_allocation_count / NULLIF(d.window_column, 0), 2) AS IpAllocations_Per_WindowId FROM AdminUpPortsWithIPs a JOIN DownPortsWindow d ON d.port_id = a.port_id ORDER BY IpAllocations_Per_WindowId DESC;

question: For ports that are DOWN and also bound to host "drive-59", list the port ID, port name, MAC address, allocated IP address, subnet ID, the average port ID window value (ordered by IP address), the tenant ID, and the running sum window of standard attribute IDs within each VIF type group, ordered by the allocated IP address. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH DownPortsWithIPs AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ia.SUBNET_ID AS subnet_id, AVG(p.ID) OVER (PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ), Drive59PortsWindow AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, p.TENANT_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE b.HOST = 'drive-59' ) SELECT d.port_id, d.port_name, d.mac_address, d.ip_address, d.subnet_id, d.window_column AS down_ports_avg_port_id_window, dr.TENANT_ID, dr.window_column AS drive59_running_sum_standard_attr_id_window FROM DownPortsWithIPs d JOIN Drive59PortsWindow dr ON dr.PORT_ID = d.port_id WHERE d.mac_address = dr.MAC_ADDRESS ORDER BY d.ip_address;

question: For IPv4 subnets, list each subnet route’s destination and next hop along with the subnet name and CIDR and the allocation pool’s first and last IP, and also include (1) the dense rank of the subnet’s associated standard attribute ID ordered by the standard attribute UPDATED_AT timestamp using a window frame of the current row and the 2 preceding rows, and (2) the dense rank within each subnet (partitioned by subnet ID) ordered by the subnet ID. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH SubnetStdAttrWindow AS ( SELECT s.NAME, dense_rank() OVER ( ORDER BY sa.UPDATED_AT ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES AS sa ON sa.ID = s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ), SubnetRoutesPoolsWindow AS ( SELECT r.DESTINATION, r.NEXTHOP, s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.SUBNET_ID ORDER BY r.SUBNET_ID) AS window_column FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ) SELECT srpw.subnet_name, srpw.subnet_cidr, srpw.DESTINATION, srpw.NEXTHOP, srpw.FIRST_IP, srpw.LAST_IP, ssaw.window_column AS std_attr_dense_rank_updated_at_window, srpw.window_column AS route_dense_rank_within_subnet FROM SubnetRoutesPoolsWindow srpw JOIN SubnetStdAttrWindow ssaw ON srpw.subnet_name = ssaw.NAME;

question: For each tenant and VIF type, among ports that are administratively up (and where the administratively-up port windowed average standard attribute ID is greater than 0), show the tenant ID, VIF type, the number of distinct administratively-up ports, the number of distinct DOWN ports that have allocated IP addresses, and whether the tenant/VIF type has any DOWN ports with IPs. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH AdminUpPorts AS ( SELECT b.PORT_ID, b.HOST, b.VIF_TYPE, b.VNIC_TYPE, p.TENANT_ID, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, AVG(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY b.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS AS b JOIN PORTS AS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 ), DownPortsWithIPs AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT aup.TENANT_ID, aup.VIF_TYPE, COUNT(DISTINCT aup.PORT_ID) AS Admin_Up_Port_Count, COUNT(DISTINCT dpi.port_id) AS Down_Port_Count, CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT dpi.port_id) > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS Has_Down_Ports_With_IPs FROM AdminUpPorts aup LEFT JOIN DownPortsWithIPs dpi ON aup.TENANT_ID = dpi.tenant_id AND aup.VIF_TYPE = dpi.vif_type WHERE aup.window_column > 0 GROUP BY aup.TENANT_ID, aup.VIF_TYPE ORDER BY Admin_Up_Port_Count DESC, Down_Port_Count DESC;

question: For subnets whose network has a RBAC action of 'access_as_shared', and where each subnet name/gateway IP group has a maximum IP version greater than 3, list the subnet name, gateway IP, CIDR, RBAC target tenant, that group’s maximum IP version, the running sum of subnet standard attribute IDs within each IP version group ordered by standard attribute ID, and the normalized value of that running sum divided by the maximum IP version (rounded to 2 decimals).
SQL: WITH SubnetWindow AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, n.TARGET_TENANT AS rbac_target_tenant, SUM(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY s.IP_VERSION ORDER BY s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN NETWORKRBACS AS n ON n.OBJECT_ID = s.NETWORK_ID WHERE n.ACTION = 'access_as_shared' ), SubnetMaxIP AS ( SELECT s.name, MAX(s.ip_version) AS max_ip_version, s.gateway_ip FROM NETWORKRBACS n JOIN SUBNETS s ON n.object_id = s.network_id WHERE n.action = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY s.name, s.gateway_ip HAVING MAX(s.ip_version) > 3 ) SELECT sw.subnet_name, sm.gateway_ip, sw.subnet_cidr, sw.rbac_target_tenant, sm.max_ip_version, sw.window_column, ROUND(sw.window_column / NULLIF(sm.max_ip_version, 0), 2) AS window_per_max_ip_version FROM SubnetWindow sw JOIN SubnetMaxIP sm ON sw.subnet_name = sm.name ORDER BY window_per_max_ip_version DESC;

question: List subnet-level insights by stacking (1) IPv4 subnets’ average and variance of DNS nameserver order values (grouped by subnet name) and (2) subnet name/gateway IP pairs whose network is shared via RBAC action 'access_as_shared' and whose maximum IP version is greater than 3, labeling each row with the reason it was included. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH DnsOrderStatsBySubnet AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, AVG(d.ORDER) AS avg_dns_order, VARIANCE(d.ORDER) AS dns_order_variance FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.ID = d.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY dns_order_variance DESC ), SharedNetworkSubnetMaxIpVersion AS ( SELECT s.name, MAX(s.ip_version) AS max_ip_version, s.gateway_ip FROM NETWORKRBACS n JOIN SUBNETS s ON n.object_id = s.network_id WHERE n.action = 'access_as_shared' GROUP BY s.name, s.gateway_ip HAVING MAX(s.ip_version) > 3 ), CombinedSubnetInsights AS ( SELECT d.subnet_name AS subnet_name, NULL AS gateway_ip, d.avg_dns_order AS avg_dns_order, d.dns_order_variance AS dns_order_variance, NULL AS max_ip_version, 'IPv4 DNS Order Stats' AS reason FROM DnsOrderStatsBySubnet d UNION ALL SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, s.gateway_ip AS gateway_ip, NULL AS avg_dns_order, NULL AS dns_order_variance, s.max_ip_version AS max_ip_version, 'Shared Network (Max IP Version > 3)' AS reason FROM SharedNetworkSubnetMaxIpVersion s ) SELECT subnet_name, gateway_ip, avg_dns_order, dns_order_variance, max_ip_version, reason FROM CombinedSubnetInsights ORDER BY subnet_name, reason;

question: Find ports whose MAC address appears in both (1) ports that are administratively up (with their port name, MAC address, port security enabled flag, and a row number ordered by MAC address using a 2-preceding/1-following window frame) and (2) ports whose status is DOWN (with their port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, and the running sum of standard attribute IDs within each resource type ordered by standard attribute ID). Return the combined results ordered by MAC address and port ID. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH DownPortsWithStdAttrWindow AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(sa.ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sa.RESOURCE_TYPE ORDER BY sa.ID ) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), AdminUpPortsWithSecurityRowNum AS ( SELECT p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED AS port_security_enabled, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 ) SELECT a.port_name, a.mac_address, a.port_security_enabled, a.window_column AS admin_up_row_number_window, d.port_id, d.tenant_id, d.window_column AS down_ports_stdattr_running_sum FROM AdminUpPortsWithSecurityRowNum a JOIN DownPortsWithStdAttrWindow d ON a.mac_address = d.mac_address ORDER BY a.mac_address, d.port_id;

question: For ports that are DOWN and are also bound to the security group ID 0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c, show the port ID, tenant ID, MAC address, port status, and allocated IP address, along with (1) the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within each security group (ordered by standard attribute ID) and (2) the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within each network (ordered by standard attribute ID). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH Subq1 AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), Subq2 AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.STATUS AS port_status, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS sgpb JOIN PORTS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID = '0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c' ) SELECT s1.port_id, s1.tenant_id, s1.mac_address, s2.port_status, s2.ip_address, s1.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_security_group, s2.window_column AS running_sum_standard_attr_id_within_network FROM Subq1 s1 JOIN Subq2 s2 ON s1.port_id = s2.port_id ORDER BY s1.port_id;

question: For IPv4 subnets, list each subnet’s name, tenant ID, network ID, IP version, CIDR, gateway IP, DHCP enabled flag, and allocation pool first/last IP, along with the maximum subnet standard attribute ID over the current subnet row and the next two rows (ordered by subnet ID). Also show any associated subnet routes (destination and next hop) and the dense-rank value within each subnet for those routes. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH SubnetDetails AS (SELECT s.NAME, s.TENANT_ID, s.NETWORK_ID, s.IP_VERSION, s.CIDR, s.GATEWAY_IP, s.ENABLE_DHCP, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, MAX(s.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( ORDER BY s.ID ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 2 FOLLOWING ) AS max_standard_attr_id_next2 FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS AS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4), SubnetRouteDetails AS (SELECT r.DESTINATION, r.NEXTHOP, s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.SUBNET_ID ORDER BY r.SUBNET_ID) AS window_column FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4) SELECT sd.NAME AS subnet_name, sd.TENANT_ID, sd.NETWORK_ID, sd.IP_VERSION, sd.CIDR, sd.GATEWAY_IP, sd.ENABLE_DHCP, sd.FIRST_IP AS allocation_first_ip, sd.LAST_IP AS allocation_last_ip, sd.max_standard_attr_id_next2, srd.DESTINATION AS route_destination, srd.NEXTHOP AS route_nexthop, srd.window_column AS route_dense_rank_within_subnet FROM SubnetDetails sd LEFT JOIN SubnetRouteDetails srd ON sd.NAME = srd.subnet_name AND sd.CIDR = srd.subnet_cidr AND sd.FIRST_IP = srd.FIRST_IP AND sd.LAST_IP = srd.LAST_IP ORDER BY sd.NAME, srd.window_column, srd.DESTINATION;

question: For each host and port status where the port has an allowed address pair with IP address 10.232.210.41/8 and the highest port standard attribute ID in that host/status group is greater than 1, return the host name, the port status, that maximum standard attribute ID, and the variance of standard attribute IDs for that same status across ports that have an IP allocation. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH HostPortMaxAttr AS ( SELECT b.HOST, MAX(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS max_standard_attr_id, p.STATUS FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN ALLOWEDADDRESSPAIRS a ON p.ID = a.PORT_ID WHERE a.IP_ADDRESS = '10.232.210.41/8' GROUP BY b.HOST, p.STATUS HAVING MAX(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) > 1 ), StatusAttrVariance AS ( SELECT p.STATUS, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM PORTS AS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.STATUS ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC ) SELECT hpma.HOST, hpma.STATUS, hpma.max_standard_attr_id, sav.standard_attr_id_variance FROM HostPortMaxAttr hpma JOIN StatusAttrVariance sav ON hpma.STATUS = sav.STATUS;

question: For active networks that have admin_state_up = 1 and at least one DOWN port, return the tenant ID, network ID, network name, admin_state_up flag, MTU, the network’s standard attribute updated_at timestamp, and the count of DOWN ports on that network. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH DownPorts AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), ActiveNetworks AS ( SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' ) SELECT an.tenant_id, an.network_id, an.network_name, an.admin_state_up, an.mtu, an.standard_attr_updated_at, COUNT(DISTINCT dp.port_id) AS down_port_count FROM ActiveNetworks an LEFT JOIN DownPorts dp ON dp.network_id = an.network_id AND dp.tenant_id = an.tenant_id WHERE an.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY an.tenant_id, an.network_id, an.network_name, an.admin_state_up, an.mtu, an.standard_attr_updated_at HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT dp.port_id) > 0 ORDER BY down_port_count DESC, an.network_name;

question: For ports that are DOWN, list the port name, network ID, MAC address, admin state, status, device owner, the bound security group ID, and the minimum admin_state_up value in a window of 3 preceding and 1 following row ordered by port ID, and also include (for the DOWN status) the coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) (standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) divided by average) of the length of allocated IP address strings for ports that have port security enabled. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH PortStatusIPLenCV AS (SELECT p.status, STDDEV(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) / NULLIF(AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)), 0) AS coefficient_of_variation FROM portsecuritybindings psb JOIN ports p ON psb.port_id = p.id JOIN ipallocations ia ON p.id = ia.port_id WHERE psb.port_security_enabled = 1 GROUP BY p.status HAVING AVG(LENGTH(ia.ip_address)) > 0 ORDER BY coefficient_of_variation DESC), DownPortsWithSecurityGroup AS (SELECT p.NAME, p.NETWORK_ID, p.MAC_ADDRESS, p.ADMIN_STATE_UP, p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER, s.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, MIN(p.ADMIN_STATE_UP) OVER ( ORDER BY p.ID ROWS BETWEEN 3 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS s ON p.ID = s.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN') SELECT d.NAME, d.NETWORK_ID, d.MAC_ADDRESS, d.ADMIN_STATE_UP, d.STATUS, d.DEVICE_OWNER, d.SECURITY_GROUP_ID, d.window_column, cv.coefficient_of_variation AS status_ip_length_coefficient_of_variation FROM DownPortsWithSecurityGroup d JOIN PortStatusIPLenCV cv ON d.STATUS = cv.status ORDER BY cv.coefficient_of_variation DESC, d.NAME;

question: For ports that are DOWN and also administratively up, list the port ID, port name, MAC address, allocated IP address, subnet ID, the per-port windowed average port ID (ordered by IP address), the tenant ID, the number of port security bindings, the total number of times port security is enabled across those bindings, and the port-security-enabled ratio (enabled total divided by binding count), ordered by the ratio descending and then by IP address.
SQL: WITH DownPortsWithIPs AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ia.SUBNET_ID AS subnet_id, AVG(p.ID) OVER (PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ), AdminUpPortSecurity AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ) SELECT d.port_id, d.port_name, d.mac_address, d.ip_address, d.subnet_id, d.window_column, a.tenant_id, a.binding_count, a.port_security_enabled_total, ROUND(a.port_security_enabled_total / NULLIF(a.binding_count, 0), 2) AS Port_Security_Enabled_Ratio FROM DownPortsWithIPs d JOIN AdminUpPortSecurity a ON d.port_id = a.port_id ORDER BY Port_Security_Enabled_Ratio DESC, d.ip_address;

question: For IPv4 subnets, list each subnet route’s destination and next hop along with the subnet name and CIDR, the allocation pool’s first and last IP, and the dense rank within each subnet; also include, for that subnet name, the range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the number of routes per subnet, ordering results by the route-count range descending. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH sq1 AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, MAX(route_count) - MIN(route_count) AS route_count_range, VARIANCE(route_count) AS route_count_variance, STDDEV(route_count) AS route_count_stddev FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN ( SELECT sr.SUBNET_ID, COUNT(*) AS route_count FROM SUBNETROUTES AS sr GROUP BY sr.SUBNET_ID, sr.NEXTHOP ) AS route_stats ON s.ID = route_stats.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY route_count_range DESC ), sq2 AS ( SELECT r.DESTINATION, r.NEXTHOP, s.NAME AS subnet_name, s.CIDR AS subnet_cidr, p.FIRST_IP, p.LAST_IP, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY r.SUBNET_ID ORDER BY r.SUBNET_ID) AS window_column FROM SUBNETROUTES r JOIN SUBNETS s ON r.SUBNET_ID = s.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONPOOLS p ON s.ID = p.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 ) SELECT sq2.subnet_name, sq2.subnet_cidr, sq2.DESTINATION, sq2.NEXTHOP, sq2.FIRST_IP, sq2.LAST_IP, sq2.window_column, sq1.route_count_range, sq1.route_count_variance, sq1.route_count_stddev FROM sq2 JOIN sq1 ON sq2.subnet_name = sq1.subnet_name ORDER BY sq1.route_count_range DESC, sq2.subnet_name, sq2.window_column;

question: For each port status and device owner (considering only ports whose standard attribute resource type is 'ports'), show the total number of ports and the earliest standard-attribute updated timestamp, along with the number of administratively-up ports and the total count of port-security bindings and enabled port-security occurrences across those admin-up ports. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH subq1 AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(p.ID) AS port_count, MIN(sa.UPDATED_AT) AS earliest_standard_attr_update FROM PORTS p JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ), subq2 AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ), subq2_rollup AS ( SELECT p.STATUS AS port_status, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, COUNT(DISTINCT s2.port_id) AS admin_up_port_count, SUM(s2.binding_count) AS total_binding_count, SUM(s2.port_security_enabled_total) AS total_port_security_enabled FROM subq2 s2 JOIN PORTS p ON p.ID = s2.port_id JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE sa.RESOURCE_TYPE = 'ports' GROUP BY p.STATUS, p.DEVICE_OWNER ) SELECT s1.port_status, s1.device_owner, s1.port_count, s1.earliest_standard_attr_update, COALESCE(r.admin_up_port_count, 0) AS admin_up_port_count, COALESCE(r.total_binding_count, 0) AS total_binding_count, COALESCE(r.total_port_security_enabled, 0) AS total_port_security_enabled FROM subq1 s1 LEFT JOIN subq2_rollup r ON r.port_status = s1.port_status AND r.device_owner = s1.device_owner ORDER BY s1.port_count DESC;

question: For ports that are DOWN, and that share a MAC address with a port that is administratively up, return the DOWN port’s ID, tenant ID, MAC address, the running sum of its standard attribute ID within its security group, plus the administratively-up port’s name, port security enabled flag, and its MAC-address-ordered row number; only include rows where the running-sum value is greater than 0. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH DownPortsBySecurityGroup AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), AdminUpPortsWithRowNumbers AS ( SELECT p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, psb.PORT_SECURITY_ENABLED AS port_security_enabled, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY p.MAC_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM PORTS AS p JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.ADMIN_STATE_UP = 1 ) SELECT dpsg.port_id, dpsg.tenant_id, dpsg.mac_address, dpsg.window_column AS down_ports_running_sum_standard_attr_id, aup.port_name, aup.port_security_enabled, aup.window_column AS admin_up_ports_row_number FROM DownPortsBySecurityGroup dpsg JOIN AdminUpPortsWithRowNumbers aup ON dpsg.mac_address = aup.mac_address WHERE dpsg.window_column > 0 ORDER BY dpsg.window_column DESC, dpsg.mac_address;

question: For each port status, list the status, the variance of the standard attribute ID across ports that have an IP allocation, and the range, variance, and standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the number of port security bindings per port (considering only ports that have at least one port security binding). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH PortStandardAttrVarianceByStatus AS ( SELECT p.STATUS, VARIANCE(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) AS standard_attr_id_variance FROM PORTS AS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS AS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.STATUS ORDER BY standard_attr_id_variance DESC ), PortSecurityBindingStatsByStatus AS ( SELECT p.status, MAX(ps.binding_count) - MIN(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_range, VARIANCE(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_variance, STDDEV(ps.binding_count) AS binding_count_stddev FROM ports AS p JOIN ( SELECT p2.id AS port_id, COUNT(*) AS binding_count FROM ports AS p2 JOIN portsecuritybindings AS b ON p2.id = b.port_id GROUP BY p2.id ) AS ps ON p.id = ps.port_id GROUP BY p.status ORDER BY binding_count_range DESC ) SELECT psav.STATUS, psav.standard_attr_id_variance, psbs.binding_count_range, psbs.binding_count_variance, psbs.binding_count_stddev FROM PortStandardAttrVarianceByStatus psav JOIN PortSecurityBindingStatsByStatus psbs ON psav.STATUS = psbs.status ORDER BY psav.standard_attr_id_variance DESC;

question: For ports whose status is DOWN, which port IDs (with their tenant ID, host, VIF type, port name, MAC address, allocated IP address, and subnet ID) appear when combining (1) the row number over IP address using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row and (2) the average port ID within each port ID group ordered by IP address? Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH down_ports_bindings AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, b.HOST AS host, b.VIF_TYPE AS vif_type, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER ( ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND 1 FOLLOWING ) AS window_column FROM ML2_PORT_BINDINGS b JOIN PORTS p ON b.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), down_ports_ipavg AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ia.SUBNET_ID AS subnet_id, AVG(p.ID) OVER (PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ) SELECT dpb.port_id, dpb.tenant_id, dpb.host, dpb.vif_type, dpb.ip_address, dpb.window_column AS row_number_by_ip_window, dpi.port_name, dpi.mac_address, dpi.subnet_id, dpi.window_column AS avg_port_id_by_ip_window FROM down_ports_bindings dpb JOIN down_ports_ipavg dpi ON dpb.port_id = dpi.port_id AND dpb.ip_address = dpi.ip_address;

question: For ports with status equal to 'DOWN', show the port ID, tenant ID, port name, network ID, MAC address, device owner, allocated IP address, subnet ID, the average port ID within each port ID group ordered by IP address, and the row number within each network ordered by port ID. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH DownPortIpWindow AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ia.SUBNET_ID AS subnet_id, AVG(p.ID) OVER (PARTITION BY p.ID ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ORDER BY ia.IP_ADDRESS ), DownPortNetworkRowNum AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.NAME AS port_name, p.NETWORK_ID AS network_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, p.DEVICE_OWNER AS device_owner, ia.IP_ADDRESS AS ip_address, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.NETWORK_ID ORDER BY p.ID) AS window_column FROM PORTS p JOIN IPALLOCATIONS ia ON p.ID = ia.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ) SELECT dpiw.port_id, dpnr.tenant_id, dpiw.port_name, dpnr.network_id, dpiw.mac_address, dpnr.device_owner, dpiw.ip_address, dpiw.subnet_id, dpiw.window_column AS avg_port_id_within_port_id_group_by_ip, dpnr.window_column AS row_number_within_network_by_port_id FROM DownPortIpWindow dpiw JOIN DownPortNetworkRowNum dpnr ON dpiw.port_id = dpnr.port_id AND dpiw.ip_address = dpnr.ip_address ORDER BY dpnr.network_id, dpnr.window_column, dpiw.ip_address;

question: For IPv4 subnets, list the subnet name along with the DNS nameserver order range, order variance, average DNS order, and DNS order variance, but only for subnets where the order variance is more than 75% of the DNS order variance. Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH SubnetOrderRangeVariance AS ( SELECT s.name AS subnet_name, MAX(d.ORDER) - MIN(d.ORDER) AS order_range, VARIANCE(d.ORDER) AS order_variance FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.id = d.subnet_id WHERE s.ip_version = 4 GROUP BY s.name ORDER BY order_range DESC ), SubnetAvgVariance AS ( SELECT s.NAME AS subnet_name, AVG(d.ORDER) AS avg_dns_order, VARIANCE(d.ORDER) AS dns_order_variance FROM SUBNETS AS s JOIN DNSNAMESERVERS AS d ON s.ID = d.SUBNET_ID WHERE s.IP_VERSION = 4 GROUP BY s.NAME ORDER BY dns_order_variance DESC ) SELECT sorv.subnet_name, sorv.order_range, sorv.order_variance, sav.avg_dns_order, sav.dns_order_variance FROM SubnetOrderRangeVariance sorv JOIN SubnetAvgVariance sav ON sorv.subnet_name = sav.subnet_name WHERE (sorv.order_variance * 1.0 / NULLIF(sav.dns_order_variance, 0)) > 0.75;

question: How many ports are both DOWN (with a running sum of STANDARD_ATTR_ID within each security group) and administratively up (with port security binding counts and total enabled port security), matching on port ID, tenant ID, and MAC address? Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH down_ports_window AS ( SELECT p.ID AS port_id, p.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, p.MAC_ADDRESS AS mac_address, SUM(p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID) OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.SECURITY_GROUP_ID ORDER BY p.STANDARD_ATTR_ID ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.PORT_ID = p.ID JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.ID = psb.PORT_ID WHERE p.STATUS = 'DOWN' ), admin_up_ports_security AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, COUNT(psb.port_id) AS binding_count, SUM(CASE WHEN psb.port_security_enabled THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS port_security_enabled_total FROM ports p JOIN portsecuritybindings psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.admin_state_up = 1 GROUP BY p.id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address ) SELECT COUNT(*) AS down_ports_with_admin_up_security_count FROM down_ports_window dpw JOIN admin_up_ports_security aups ON dpw.port_id = aups.port_id AND dpw.tenant_id = aups.tenant_id AND dpw.mac_address = aups.mac_address;

question: For ACTIVE networks, list each network’s ID, name, tenant ID, admin_state_up flag, MTU, and standard-attribute updated_at timestamp, along with any DOWN ports on that network (port ID and MAC address), the port’s security group ID, the port’s rank within its security group (ordered by port ID), and the network’s row number within its tenant (ordered by network name). Do not return any rounded answers.
SQL: WITH q1 AS ( SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.tenant_id, p.mac_address, sgpb.security_group_id, RANK() OVER ( PARTITION BY sgpb.security_group_id ORDER BY p.id ) AS window_column FROM SECURITYGROUPPORTBINDINGS AS sgpb JOIN PORTS AS p ON sgpb.port_id = p.id JOIN PORTSECURITYBINDINGS AS psb ON p.id = psb.port_id WHERE p.status = 'DOWN' ), q2 AS ( SELECT n.ID AS network_id, n.NAME AS network_name, n.TENANT_ID AS tenant_id, n.ADMIN_STATE_UP AS admin_state_up, n.MTU AS mtu, sa.UPDATED_AT AS standard_attr_updated_at, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY n.TENANT_ID ORDER BY n.NAME) AS window_column FROM NETWORKS n JOIN STANDARDATTRIBUTES sa ON sa.ID = n.STANDARD_ATTR_ID WHERE n.STATUS = 'ACTIVE' ) SELECT q2.network_id, q2.network_name, q2.tenant_id, q2.admin_state_up, q2.mtu, q2.standard_attr_updated_at, q1.port_id, q1.mac_address, q1.security_group_id, q1.window_column AS port_rank_within_security_group, q2.window_column AS network_row_number_within_tenant FROM q2 JOIN PORTS p ON p.network_id = q2.network_id JOIN q1 ON q1.port_id = p.id AND q1.tenant_id = q2.tenant_id ORDER BY q2.tenant_id, q2.network_name, q1.security_group_id, q1.window_column, q1.port_id;

question: List all ports that are administratively up, including (1) ports that are administratively up with their host, VIF/VNIC types, tenant/network IDs, MAC, status, device owner, and the average standard attribute ID over a 2-preceding/2-following window by VIF type, and (2) ports that are administratively up but have status = 'DOWN' with their port name, allocated IP address, subnet ID, and the average port ID window value ordered by IP address; include a “reason” column indicating whether each row comes from “Admin State Up” or “Status DOWN”. Do not return any rounded answers.
